Separate augmentation does not suffice for parallel pairs; cross-consequences such as R must be added or linked components augmented jointly. | Conjecture; exact checks for h <= 5 (W for h <= 4). | [Shared-input falls entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-24-shared-input-falls) |
| `ex:pairwise-augmentation-triple-falls` | Pairwise augmentation, triple falls: over F_3, three complete accuracy-one ENS blocks with h inputs and private coefficients, linked either as a parallel triple (first inputs x, x+1, x+2) or as a chain (a, b share x; b, c share another form; a, c share nothing), with every pair jointly Groebner-augmented (homogenized pairwise joint dp bases plus field equations), still fall in their span ring below degree 11: lowest fall at degree 6 for h = 2 and 9 for h = 3 in both configurations. | `lem:chain-consequences` | Chain consequences: over F_3, for a chain of k >= 2 complete accuracy-one ENS blocks with h >= 2 inputs, consecutive blocks sharing one identical affine input lambda_m, E_k = F G_{k-1} ... G_2 P_{b_1} vanishes on the chain's zero set, where F = q_u prod L_{w_j} (1 - r_u) (end block, degree h+1) forces lambda_{k-1} true, G_m = (1 - r_{lambda_m}) prod L_{w_j} (degree h-1) passes truth from lambda_m to lambda_{m-1}, and P_{b_1} vanishes once lambda_1 is true; deg E_k = h + 4 + (k-2)(h-1). Expanding 1 = q + L^2 at lambda_1 puts z^2 E_k in the joint augmentation of the two (k-1)-subchains, so the chain falls at degree <= deg E_k + 1 unless E_k lies there in its own degree. Independence of other inputs and private coefficients are not used. For h >= D - 3 every E_k exceeds D; this locates the known witness only (lower falls exist at h = 2). | `prop:fiber-decomposition-bounds` | Fiber decomposition bounds: over F_p modulo field equations, for two constraint systems a, b (ideals containing the field equations) in variables (x_V, Y_a), (x_V, Y_b) with Y_a, Y_b disjoint (non-shared forms and private variables jointly independent, after an affine change over F_p), J the z-homogenization of their separate degree-order bases: (1) every polynomial of degree s vanishing on the joint zero set lies in (I_a T)_{<= s+(p-1)\|V\|} + (I_b T)_{<= s+(p-1)\|V\|} (T the full ring mod field equations) (Lagrange idempotents in x_V plus degree-compatible splitting of each fiber in disjoint variables), so z^{(p-1)\|V\|} kills every z-torsion element; (2) with m_a, m_b the least degrees of nonzero elements of the fiber sums K_a = sum_v I(Z_a^v), K_b, there is no fall of J in degrees below m_a + m_b (top parts of the interpolation coefficients lie in gr(K_a) gr(K_b)). (3) For complete accuracy-one ENS blocks over F_3 sharing one linear part (identical or parallel), m_a = m_b = 2 (r_1^2 - r_1 vanishes on the fiber intersection), so (2) gives only no fall below 4, while observed falls start at 5 to 8. | `thm:parallel-pair-fall` | Parallel pair fall: over F_3, two complete accuracy-one ENS blocks a, b with h_a, h_b >= 2 inputs and private coefficients, parallel inputs x + c_a, x + c_b (c_a != c_b), other inputs independent, each Groebner-augmented separately, fall at degree 7: R = P_a P_b (q_a - q_b) is not in J in degree 7 while z R is, provided a's false-fiber ideal (its (h_a - 1)-input block, r_{a,1} free) has no nonzero element of degree <= 3 and m(I_a^T) + m(I_b^F) >= 8. | `lem:section-retraction` | Section retraction: over F_3, in a family F of separately Groebner-augmented complete accuracy-one ENS blocks with private coefficients, inputs either affine forms in shared coordinates or private coordinates, cross generators R_ab = P_a P_b (q_a - q_b), T_abc = P_a P_b P_c and W = F_b P_a chosen by a rule on the involved blocks, and field equations, substituting the standard section (a private input y_j = 0, r_j = 1, other private inputs 1, other coefficients 0) of a block B with a private input maps J_s(F) into J_s(F \ B) for every s. | `lem:leaf-reduction` | Leaf reduction: over F_3 (also F_q), for a family F of systems (ideals in their private variables and the shared coordinates they read, pairwise disjoint private variables, no cross generators) and a system a reading exactly one shared coordinate x, with U any set of other systems, R = F \ a, and M_U, M_W the top ideals of U and R \ U in the truncated algebra A_R of x and R's variables: if x^alpha A_R cap (M_U + M_W) = (x^alpha A_R cap M_U) + x^alpha M_W for alpha = 1, 2 (a modular law over the chain ring F_3[x]/(x^3); it fails even for ideals, e.g. A_R = S[y]/(y^3), M_U = (x+y), M_W = (y)), then every degree at which F falls (in the family's algebra) is one at which {a} cup U or R falls. | `lem:adapted-basis-criterion` | Adapted-basis criterion: over S = k[x]/(x^n) (k a field), for a finite family Sigma of submodules of a finitely generated free S-module F, with C the colon modules (M : x^j), M in Sigma, 0 <= j <= n, and phi(A) = (A + xF)/xF, the following are equivalent: (a) Sigma has a common adapted basis (F = sum S e_i, each M = sum x^{a_i(M)} S e_i); (b) (i) phi preserves finite intersections of members of C and (ii) the phi(C) generate a distributive lattice of subspaces of F/xF; (c) C together with xF generates a distributive lattice of submodules. | `prop:shared-form-obstruction` | Shared-form obstruction: over a field of characteristic p >= 3, for Q a nonempty subset of a set of 0/1 points with graded functions gr F^Q and an F_p-valued affine form l (top l-bar, l-bar^p = 0), if phi(l)*psi vanishes on Q with deg phi = alpha <= p-1 and psi of degree beta with top psi-bar, then freeness of gr F^Q over F[t]/(t^p) (t -> l-bar) in degrees <= alpha+beta forces psi-bar in l-bar^(p-alpha) gr_(alpha+beta-p) F^Q (zero when alpha+beta < p); otherwise gr F^Q is not free in those degrees over Lambda (x) T for any truncated algebra T of form tops containing l-bar, so lem:filtered-freeness-transfer cannot be applied with l among its forms. | `lem:shared-link` | Shared link: over a field of characteristic p, on a set of 0/1 points with row sums, for F_p-valued affine forms b (functions R, gr R = T_R), a value set W, and Lambda' a truncated algebra acting through tops of F_p-valued degree-1 functions (the rows, possibly more forms): if X = Q' cup B with B = X cap {b in W} and X minus Q' inside {b in W}, gr F^{Q'} is free below n_0 over T_R (x) Lambda' in the sense of lem:filtered-freeness-transfer, and gr F^B agrees below n_0 with a free Lambda'-module, then so does gr F^X; with Lambda' containing the row-sum algebra, X is row-free through n_0 - 1. Corollary (clause step): if gr F^Q and gr F^{Q cap S} are free below n_0 over T_R (x) Lambda', then Q cap (S cup {b in W}) is. So a clause joining a shared-form condition S to forms b needs freeness over b only. If the W_X have Tor_1 = 0 through D (true for N - D >= (p-1)D^2 by the free-seed argument), the Koszul hypothesis of thm:closure-gluing through D holds iff (L): A_e cap r tilde V_e = r A_e in degrees <= D for every e. Corollary (no freeness hypothesis needed): if every link's vanishing tops of degree <= D are the sub-slice's own, Z satisfies the hypothesis iff the slice does (which thm:weak-base-stability-quadratic gives for N >= (p-1)D^2). Proof: split A~ by the cells blocked through their columns into summands Lambda_{U - B} (x) V' (x) Rest on which tau acts as the restricted top; the tensor-kernel formula and Wilson's mod-3 ranks of inclusion matrices give ker l^2 = l Lambda_j (m >= 2j+2) and ker l = l^2 Lambda_j (m >= 2j+1); lem:spare-column-transfer removes the row sums. On the padded hole family (blocks: real input X_{jt}-1 plus k fillers F_s = R_{n+1} + (R_{j_s} - 1), R_j the row sums, which vanish at psi and equal 1 modulo the base) the rule must exclude X_{n+1,t}-1 for every hole t, whatever its tie-break; the filler prefix reduces to 1 at degree about 2k+2, each clause gives x_{n+1,t} = 0, and pigeon n+1's row equation refutes at degree about 2(k+1). | `prop:rigid-form-reduction` | Rigid-form reduction: over F_p (p odd), call an affine form L rigid at degree D0 if 1 - L^{p-1} lies in the degree-D0 PC closure of the weak unary base B. Padding by base-rigid fillers (2-X_v, C_s-2, R_{n+1}+R_j-1) therefore cannot refute W; forms rigid only modulo other clauses or only above D - (p-1)k, and rarely-zero non-rigid forms, are not removed. | Working proof (elementary closure bookkeeping), reviewed by a fresh-context reviewer; an equivalent reformulation of W that does not advance its hardness. | [Rigid forms entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-25-rigid-forms) |

| `lem:per-order-value-arithmetic` | Consequences of Phi(n,k,l) = n + 2l + sum_{j<n} floor((k-l-1)/2^j): with k-l-1 = q 2^n + r, Phi + 2q + s_2(r) = n + 2(k-1); Phi and the construction lie below n+2k-2-s_2(k-l-1) when k-l-1 >= 2^n; Phi(n,k+2^n,l) = Phi + 2^(n+1) - 2; Phi = n+2k-2-s_2(k-l-1) for k-1 <= n; Phi(n,k,k-1) = n+2k-2; Phi(n+1,k,l) = Phi + 1 + floor((k-l-1)/2^n); the construction has degree exactly Phi; the examples; F has 2^n - 1 factors and F^2 multiplicity >= 2^n, degree <= 2^(n+1)-2; mult_a(P) <= ord P(a+z); and these facts for the least degree delta(n,k,l) itself; in one variable Phi(1,k,l) = k + l = delta(1,k,l). | Working proof, verified in Lean (PerOrderArithmetic.lean), from the Legendre form, the digit-sum identities, per_order_value and the hyperplane-product lemma. | [Lean: every side claim of the preprint](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-lean-preprint-side-claims), [novelty check](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-25-novelty-check) |

| `cor:block-amplification` | Block amplification: for forms whose column parts are independent and identically distributed across disjoint blocks, degree h+1 directness of B product tops on N columns fails with probability at most (1 - g_q(B))^{floor(N/q)}, g_q(B) the probability of the propagation theorem's hypotheses on q given columns; g_{B(2K+1)}(B) > 0 for every B (disjoint supports plus the spread lemma), so fixed B is direct with probability tending to 1 (proved rate (1 - 3^{-KmqB})^{N/q}); constant probability c at every size up to (1-eps) of the fill gives probability 1 - delta for B <= c_delta fill(N) with c_delta of order (c / log(1/delta))^4 at K = 2. | Working proof (independence of disjoint blocks plus thm:directness-propagation). | [Directness propagation entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-25-directness-propagation) |

The q = 7 certificate stayed direct in six embeddings into N = 9 with random, zero or copied extra columns. | Exact GF(3) finite check (FLINT ranks). | [Directness propagation entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-25-directness-propagation) |

With the order bound along general lines it makes the Plücker order at a double point independent of rho. | [Arc-limit saturation](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#cube-arc-limit-saturation) |
| `conj:cube-arc-limit-orders` | On {0,1}^3 in characteristic != 2, for every arc through a double point along which A_{4d} has rank 4d, every nonzero element of the arc-limit space S_gamma has T-order at most 4d. | Proved, in stronger form (every arc with nonzero distinct coordinates, every n), by thm:cube-flat-limit-order-bound; consistent with all recorded arcs (attained at d = 4 on the diagonal). | [Arc-limit saturation](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#cube-arc-limit-saturation) |

| `thm:taylor-propagation` | Taylor propagation: for a graded commutative algebra R, elements tau_b of one degree h, F_b in Ann_{R_1}(tau_b), and R' = R (x) (F + V) with V in degree 1 and V^2 = 0 (an added column), pi tau'_b = tau_b and pi F'_b containing F_b, there is an exact sequence 0 -> Syz_{e-1}(R) (x) V -> Syz_e(R') -> Syz_e(R), and the defect Def_e = dim Syz_e / T_e (T_e the Frobenius and Koszul-pair span) satisfies Def_e(R') <= dim(pi Syz_e(R') / T_e(R)) + m Def_{e-1}(R) <= Def_e(R) + m Def_{e-1}(R); so Taylor generation on one block of columns in all multiplier degrees up to e (degree 0: independent tops) gives it on every larger board. Generalises thm:directness-propagation (e = 1). The proof also works with Frobenius elements of any positive degree and chosen liftable pair syzygies, the span thm:based-taylor-glue uses; with Koszul pairs as stated, zero defect matches that hypothesis only for tops without shared forms. Defects never die: a block defect extends or reappears one degree up tensored with the new column (e.g. two tops agreeing outside column c give global syzygies v(e_b - e_b'), v in V_c). | Working proof; supported by exact rank checks at multiplier degree 2 (q = 9 blocks into N = 10, three of three). | [Taylor propagation entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-25-taylor-propagation) |
| `cor:taylor-block-amplification` | Taylor block amplification: for forms whose column parts are independent and identically distributed across disjoint blocks, Taylor generation up to multiplier degree e on N columns fails with probability at most (1 - t_q(B,e))^{floor(N/q)}, t_q the probability of zero defect up to e on q given columns; in the random model of W-shaped tops without shared forms the Koszul range of generic W reduces to constant-probability Taylor generation on blocks of about n/L columns (with the fill-fraction loss of cor:block-amplification). | Working proof (independent disjoint blocks plus thm:taylor-propagation). | [Taylor propagation entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-25-taylor-propagation) |
| `prop:one-column-pair-lifting` | One-column pair lifting: over F_3, on a base z-injective below D containing x^2 - x and the column collisions, for product constraints C, C' with the same factors h_j whose forms agree (constants included) on every cell outside column c, and a cell v of column c, v(e_C - e_C') is a signed top syzygy in degree s = \|b\|+1 <= D; it satisfies the glue induction's solvability condition for every normalised NS functional iff v(C_v - C'_v) lies in V'_{s-1}, the degree-(s-1) NS span of the base and the whole family (not containing 1), so non-lifting is exactly a degree fall; C_v sets v = 1 and the other cells of column c to 0. It lifts at cells where the forms' coefficients agree; when C_v, C'_v differ in one factor, C_v - C'_v = kappa R_v (thm:resolvent-taylor-glue's identity), so it lifts once the resolvent is in the family; several-factor differences and dependencies of three or more tops remain open. | Working proof (reduction by collisions and Booleanity inside the glue proof's solvability condition). | [One-column pairs entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-25-one-column-pairs) |
| `thm:cell-resolvents` | Cell resolvents: over F_3, in prop:one-column-pair-lifting's setting with W's normalized factors (L - a, at most one chi_a(U)), fix a cell v of column c and let T be the factors whose restricted constants shift at v. (a) If chi is shifted (with any number t of shifted linear factors), or at most two linear factors and no chi are shifted, then C_v - C'_v = kappa R_v Q_v as functions, hence modulo the base within degree s-1, with R_v an explicit product (1; delta_2 x_1 + delta_1 x_2 + delta_1 delta_2; (u - gamma) prod_j (gamma u - delta_j x_j)); the normalized cell resolvent v R_v Q_v is derived at degree s, and a family closed (degree bound D) under resolvents and these cell resolvents may add these one-column syzygies and their multiples to thm:resolvent-taylor-glue's spanning set; with D = 22k a constant in it still gives a refutation. (b) Local model: if chi is unshifted and t >= 3 linear factors shift, then with the shifted forms as independent coordinates on F_3^T, the degree-<= t-1 functions vanishing on Z = {C_v = 0 = C'_v} are the scalar multiples of w = prod x_j - prod (x_j + delta_j), w is not a product of affine and chi factors, and every such product of degree <= t-1 vanishing on Z is zero; images smaller than F_3^T, other forms and the whole allowed set are not covered. | Working proof after a fresh-context review, with exhaustive local checks of the identities (t <= 4) and of part (b) for t = 3, 4, 5. | [Cell resolvents entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-25-cell-resolvents) |
| `prop:two-block-taylor-failure` | Two-block failure: over F_3, for two W blocks of k+1 forms l_j - a_j and l_j - a'_j on the same linear forms l_1..l_{k+1} with a_j != a'_j for every j (padded by blocks of at most k forms): (1) if k >= 3 and the l_j are independent in G_1, for every prefix choice the degree-bounded resolvent saturation of the normalized clauses is the pair itself and its top syzygies (e_C - e_C' at degree \|b\| if the outside indices agree, (l_i', -l_i) at degree \|b\|+1 otherwise) are not spanned by thm:resolvent-taylor-glue's (F) and (K), so the corollary's Taylor generation hypothesis fails; (2) if the outside indices agree, and the forms meet member pinning's row hypotheses at degree \|b\|, some normalized NS functional through \|b\|-1 for the base plus the pair has mu(C - C') != 0 and does not extend, so the theorem's conclusion fails; (3) if k >= 2, W's system for the family has no PC refutation of degree 22k (cor:single-form-pinning with M' = 2). Code families of 3(k+1)+1 blocks with a distance-3 constant code (k >= 5, shortened Hamming codes) force shape (b) of thm:cell-resolvents for every prefix choice, and member pinning proves W for them; whether their saturation fails Taylor generation is open. | Working proof in a route review, after a fresh-context review and a second pass on part 2. | [Binomial route review](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-25-binomial-route-review) |
| `lem:free-vanishing-tops` | Free vanishing tops: in prop:link-criterion's setting, with Lambda_u = F[r_1..r_u]/(r_i^p) and sigma = prod r_i^(p-1), a graded module M free through d+(p-1)u has m in rM whenever sigma m = 0 (m of degree d); hence if the links' vanishing-top module A_e is free through D+(p-1)u, condition (L) holds for e through D (no hypothesis on tilde V_e), and with (b) (N-D >= (p-1)D^2) closed row freeness through D follows; for u = 1, M is free through t iff ker r = im r^(p-1) in degrees <= t-1. Self-injectivity of Lambda_u made truncation-safe; equivalent to (L) up to a degree shift of (p-1)u, which is necessary. Separated-member gluing of closed members reaches only one degree above their least generator in its proof. | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [Free vanishing tops entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-25-free-vanishing-tops) |
| `prop:content-reduction-scope` | Content reduction scope: with Lambda_{m-1} = F[r_1..r_{m-1}]/(r_i^p) acting on gr F^P of the column-injective assignments (N holes) and (p-1)(m-1) > N (as on PHP's board, m = N+1), a vanishing-top module free through t is zero in all degrees <= t-(p-1)(m-1); so lem:free-vanishing-tops over all row sums, without a reduction to few rows, is vacuous for members with vanishing tops of degree <= D (condition (L) and the closure-gluing hypothesis are not). Remarks: in a fixed bulk basis degree-1 content grading needs a column form or a single-row form; by thm:row-rank-seeds' row change the reachable parameter is the affine row rank, heuristically O(sqrt N), while W's generic forms have rank about n. | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [Cell forms scope entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-25-cell-forms-scope) |
| `lem:hole-splitting` | Hole splitting: over any field, for any set Z of occupancy patterns and a hole j, with fibers Z^0 (c_j = 0) and Z^1 (c_j = 1) on the other holes, the vanishing-top modules of prop:link-criterion satisfy exact sequences of Lambda_u-modules 0 -> V_j (x) A_e(Z^1) -> A_e(Z) -> bar A_e -> 0 and 0 -> (A_{e-1}(Z^0) + A_{e-1}(Z^1))(-1) -> bar A_e -> A_e(Z^0) cap A_e(Z^1) -> 0 (V_j the u cells of column j in degree 1); hence A_e(Z) is free through t if A_e(Z^1) and the sum are free through t-1 and the intersection through t (extensions of modules free through t are free through t). Via lem:free-vanishing-tops (after reducing to u <= D rows), closed row freeness follows from three freeness statements on N-1 holes; the sum and intersection are not vanishing-top modules of pattern sets in general. | Working proof after a fresh-context review, with an exact check of the identifications at N = 10. | [Hole splitting entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-25-hole-splitting) |
| `conj:fiber-lattice-freeness` | Fiber lattice freeness (conjecture): over F_p, for the allowed set Z (in a slice) of W clauses on column forms, every hole j and every e, the systems A_e(Z^0) + A_e(Z^1) and A_e(Z^0) cap A_e(Z^1) of the two fibers' vanishing tops on the other N-1 holes are free over the row sums through every degree where the column tensor powers on N-1-e holes are free; with lem:hole-splitting and induction on N (the class is closed under links) it would reduce freeness of such members' vanishing tops, and via lem:free-vanishing-tops closed row freeness in this class, to a base case. Evidence: exact check at N = 10, one row, e <= 2, degrees <= 4: fibers differ at 24 to 146 links for W-like members, yet all fiber modules, sums and intersections are free in range. | Conjecture with an exact small check far below its natural range. | [Fiber uniformity entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-25-fiber-uniformity) |
| `ex:fiber-lattice-nondistributive` | Fiber lattice non-distributivity: over F_3 at N = 10 (one row, e <= 2, links \|S\| <= 2), the vanishing-top subspaces of the four fibers of a column member at two holes satisfy inclusion-exclusion (so generate a distributive lattice on triples) for the slice and a single W clause, but fail it for the two-block pair (6 triples, gap 1) and for three clauses on four forms (39-41 triples and 9-15 quadruples, gaps up to 3); refutes an adapted-basis mechanism for iterating lem:hole-splitting once clauses interact, leaving conj:fiber-lattice-freeness open. | Retracted as a refutation: the failures are confined to links with six free holes at N = 10 and vanish at N = 12 (ex:fiber-lattice-size-check); the exact data stand. | [Fiber lattice entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-25-fiber-lattice) |

So the non-distributivity recorded in ex:fiber-lattice-nondistributive is a small-size artifact. | Exact finite check refuting the general claim of ex:fiber-lattice-nondistributive (non-distributivity once clauses interact): distributive on every link at N = 12. | [Fiber lattice correction](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-25-fiber-lattice-correction) |
| `lem:atom-filtration` | Atom filtration: if graded submodules A_1..A_k of a graded Lambda_u-module generate a distributive lattice, every lattice element M = sum_{T in T} X_T (X_T = cap_{t in T} A_t, T closed under supersets) is an iterated extension of the atoms X_T / Y_T, Y_T = sum_{t not in T} (X_T cap A_t), so it is free through t when those atoms are (Birkhoff's graded pieces, applied to modules); for coefficient systems distributivity is checked link by link. Evidence: at N = 12 (F_3, one row, e = 2, two split holes) all 15 four-fiber atoms of two W-like column members are free through degree 4, with distributivity verified only on links \|S\| <= 2. Iterating lem:hole-splitting with it is a sketch needing further identities. | Working proof after a fresh-context review, with an exact small check. | [Atom filtration entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-25-atom-filtration) |
| `lem:cell-splitting` | Cell splitting: over any field, for any set Q of column-injective assignments of m rows to N holes (e.g. cut by W clauses on arbitrary cell forms) and a column j, with fibers Q^{(empty)} and Q^{(i)} (row i at column j) on the other holes and rho_j = sum_i x_ij, the vanishing tops A(Q) in the weak top algebra T have a filtration by row-sum submodules with factors (1) sum_i x_ij (x) A(Q^{(i)}), (2) rho_j (x) A(Q^{(empty)})/(A(Q^{(empty)}) cap cap_i A(Q^{(i)})), (3) cap over all states of A(Q^{(s)}); hence V(Q) = T/A(Q) is an extension of T'/cap_s A(Q^{(s)}) by (sum_i x_ij V(Q^{(i)}))/(image of factor 2), and the Koszul condition of thm:global-closure-gluing for Q through D follows from it for the row fibers through D-1, Tor_1 of T'/cap_s A(Q^{(s)}) through D, and an (L)-type injectivity for factor 2, over Lambda_{m-1} in characteristic p (the row fibers lie in occupancy class m-1); only the row-fiber condition recurses on sets, and working on the quotient side avoids the socle shift of the ideal-side route. Generalizes lem:hole-splitting (u = m-1, after a change of basis in column j) to cell forms. | Working proof after a fresh-context review, with an exact check of the dimension identity (m = 3, N = 5). | [Cell splitting entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-25-cell-splitting) |
| `cor:monotone-fiber-recursion` | Monotone fiber recursion: in lem:cell-splitting's setting, if the empty fiber's vanishing tops lie in every row fiber's, A_d(Q^{(empty)}) in A_d(Q^{(i)}) for all rows i and d <= D (cycle degree), then factor 2 vanishes, the intersection over states is A(Q^{(empty)}), and V(Q) is, in degrees <= D, an extension of V(Q^{(empty)}) by sum_i x_ij (x) V(Q^{(i)}); so the Koszul condition for Q through D follows from it for the empty fiber through D and the row fibers through D-1, a deletion-link recursion on sets. Exact checks: W-like column members at N = 10 have equal whole-fiber tops but satisfy the needed inclusion on only 9 and 4 of 36 links with \|S\| = 2 for two and three interacting clauses; cell-form sets at m = 3, N = 5 are monotone in some degrees only. | Working proof (immediate from lem:cell-splitting) after a fresh-context review, with an exact check of applicability. | [Monotone fibers entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-25-monotone-fibers) |
| `conj:good-column` | Good column (conjecture): for the allowed set Z of W clauses on column forms, and every set arising from Z by fibers and links, some hole j has a_S(Z^0_j) contained in a_S(Z^1_j) for every link S not containing j, in every degree within the free range; with cor:monotone-fiber-recursion this reduces the Koszul hypothesis of thm:global-closure-gluing for such Z to base cases along a deletion-link recursion. | Conjecture supported by an exact check at N = 12 (ex:good-columns). | [Good columns entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-25-good-columns) |
| `ex:good-columns` | Good columns check: over F_3 at N = 12 (e = 2, links \|S\| <= 2), W-like column members have holes where the monotone inclusion holds on every link: 10, 6 and 10 of 12 holes for one clause, the two-block pair and three clauses on sparse seeded forms (holes where the outside form has coefficient 2 fail everywhere), and 8 and 4 for one clause and the pair with a dense outside form; failures concentrate on links with \|S\| = 2. | Exact finite check. | [Good columns entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-25-good-columns) |
| `ex:two-step-good-columns` | Two-step good columns: over F_3 at N = 12 (e = 2, links \|S\| <= 2), after splitting at a good column the fibers on 11 holes still have good columns, but few: only the free hole for both fibers of the two-block pair with a dense outside form, and holes {4} and {7, 11} for the three clauses on sparse forms; failures at \|S\| <= 1 occur only at holes in the outside form's support, and most failures are on links with \|S\| = 2 (8 remaining holes), so conj:good-column is neither confirmed nor refuted at this size; the free hole was good in every fiber tested. | Exact finite check. | [Two-step columns entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-25-two-step-columns) |
| `prop:free-hole-counterexample` | Free hole counterexample: over F_3, a hole j outside every form's support need not be a good column for cor:monotone-fiber-recursion: with s' = sum over h != j of C_h (coefficient 0 at j) and Z = {c in the slice m : s'(c) != m}, the slice relation gives s' = m - C_j, so Z forces hole j occupied, its empty fiber is empty (all monomials vanish) and its occupied fiber is the whole slice m-1, whose tops are the multiples of s'; the inclusion fails for every e >= 1. Freeness must be taken modulo the slice (all-ones vector). | Elementary refutation, verified by hand. | [Free hole entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-25-free-hole) |
| `conj:free-hole-good` | Free hole good (conjecture): if hole j is outside every form's support and the forms' coefficient vectors on the other holes, with the all-ones vector, are linearly independent over F_3, then the two fibers at j (the same member in adjacent mod-3 slices) have equal vanishing tops on every link in every degree within the free range; equivalently j is a good column for every slice value, since inclusion around the three residues forces equality. In tension with the N=10 fiber check, which found unequal fiber tops at a free hole on links not split by size. | Conjecture; proved where the filtered freeness transfer applies (cor:free-hole-uniformity); beyond it a dense pair has unequal fiber tops at N = 12, e = 2 (ex:free-hole-transfer-check), outside every transfer range. | [Free hole entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-25-free-hole) |
| `cor:free-hole-uniformity` | Free hole uniformity: over F_p, for Z'_a = {c in {0,1}^H : sum c = a mod p, l(c) in Omega} (affine column forms l_1..l_d on H = [N] minus a hole j outside every form's support), on a link S with degree e: (i) if the graded functions Gamma_S of the cube of H minus S contain a free T-submodule (T = F[w_0..w_d]/(w^p) acting by the tops of s and the restricted forms) agreeing with Gamma_S in degrees <= e, then a_{S,e}(Z'_a) = (((w_0) + top(I_{Omega_S})) Gamma_S)_e, independent of a, so the fibers at j have equal tops and j is a good column there at every slice value; (ii) split variant: for H minus S = U + V, the same conclusion holds when the cube of V contains a free submodule, agreeing below e+1, over the algebra of s_V and only those forms not constant on V, keeping the coordinates on U exactly (the lemma's proof extended to function algebras of finite product sets, with a graph argument for the top ideal); with all forms kept, (ii) would follow from (i) by the Hopf tensor identity. Any field of characteristic p; independence from the all-ones vector is implied by (T). A corollary of lem:filtered-freeness-transfer (part (a)) with a dimension count for the top ideal of a point times a set. | Working proof after a fresh-context review; corollary of the recorded transfer lemma. | [Free hole transfer entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-26-free-hole-transfer) |
| `ex:free-hole-transfer-check` | Free hole transfer check: over F_3 at N = 12 (hole 11 free, links \|S\| <= 2, e = 1, 2), no link has hypothesis (T) with unequal fiber tops; random forms (l_0 on three holes) fail (T) on every link yet have equal fiber tops on all 67 links for one clause, the two-block pair and three clauses; a dense two-block pair has equal tops at e = 1 ((T) on 29 links) but at e = 2, where (T) holds on no link, unequal tops on 4 of 11 links with \|S\| = 1 and 34 of 55 with \|S\| = 2, outside every transfer range. | Exact finite check. | [Free hole transfer entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-26-free-hole-transfer) |
| `prop:hilbert-factorization` | Hilbert factorization: over a field of characteristic p, for functions F on a finite point set X with Gamma = gr F, polynomials lambda_1..lambda_r of degree <= 1 with F_p values and T = F[w]/(w^p) acting by their tops, if Gamma contains a free T-submodule agreeing with it below degree n_0, then for every Omega in F_p^r, H(Z_Omega) = H(Gamma) H(Omega) / H(T) mod q^{n_0} (H(Omega) the affine Hilbert series of Omega); hence size consistency relative to a shared factor, H(Z_{O0xO1xO2}) H(Z_{O0x*x*}) = H(Z_{O0xO1x*}) H(Z_{O0x*xO2}) mod q^{n_0}, and for shared forms the correction (H(Gamma)/H(T))^2 [H(OA cap OB) H(T_1) - H(OA) H(OB)].
