| `lem:spare-pigeon-composition` | Spare-pigeon composition: over F_3, for any family F of blocks on the (n+1) x n board and any pigeon s, a degree-D PC refutation of the pinned system (conj:occupancy-pinned-php, e = 2) plus F's randomized-prefix clauses gives one of degree max(D,2) of weak PHP of the n pigeons other than s into the n-2 non-empty holes plus the clauses of sigma_s(F) with the same prefix matrices, where sigma_s sets the empty holes' cells to 0 and x_sj -> 1 - sum_{i != s} x_ij; supp sigma_s(b) <= \|U_b\| + n \|U_b cap row s\|. | Working proof (composition of thm:spare-pigeon-onto-hardness's substitution with restriction), after a fresh-context review. | [Composed-pins entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-26-composed-pins) |
| `prop:light-spare-composition` | Light-spare composition (conditional): over F_3, for a family L u S fixed in advance, L light (\|U_b\| <= n^{2-eta}) and S of rank <= rho modulo the column sums, if some pigeon s has \|U_b cap row s\| <= n^{1-eta} for all b in L, then W_RS holds at degree B = max(11 max(1,delta), 4t+2) with failure probability <= \|S\| 3^{rho-t} + o(1), provided thm:random-prefix-light-families holds for weak PHP^{N+2}_N (N = n-2). Families whose heavy rows cover every pigeon row defeat the choice of s; for them the mixed case is open. | Condition discharged by thm:random-prefix-light-families-imbalance; unconditional form thm:light-column-mixed-families. | [Composed-pins entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-26-composed-pins) |
| `lem:cube-odd-generator-criterion` | On {0,1}^3 in characteristic != 2, for e >= 2, with s the solution of P_e P_{e+1} and t that of P_{e-1} P_{e+2} at (2e+1, 2): (W_e) holds iff some quartic form alpha makes F_2 divide every coordinate of t - alpha s, where F_2 is the product of the three linear forms y1 +- y2 +- y3 through the double points; equivalently the ratio t/s on each of the three lines, where c is 2-torsion, is a binary quartic and the three agree at the double points. | Working proof from lem:cube-general-peeling, lem:cube-boundary-generators-coprime, lem:cube-excess-sum-basis and lem:cube-threshold-ideal; reviewed by a fresh-context referee. | [Odd generator criterion](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-odd-generator-criterion) |
| `check:cube-odd-generator-seven-two` | Over F_1000003 the S_3-invariant witnesses of excess 24 at (7,2), m = 29, form a 2-dimensional space whose solutions have value rank 2 at a random point, so (W_3) holds modulo the computing prime with an invariant generator. | Finite check by the chunked sym val mode of bmd_cube_solution_cones (FLINT), validated on (3,2) and (5,2); no rational lift. | [Odd generator criterion](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-odd-generator-criterion) |
| `lem:cube-odd-generator-poles` | On {0,1}^3 in characteristic != 2, for e >= 2 and each line l of F_2 = 0: the ratio lambda_l = t/s of the solutions of P_{e-1}P_{e+2} and P_e P_{e+1} at (2e+1,2) is regular on l except possibly at its four collision points (two double points and two further points) and at the finite sets Z_e, Z_{e+1} where boundary solutions vanish; on l outside Z_2 and the relevant Z_n, where c is 2-torsion, phi_{n+2} = mu_n psi phi_n for a fixed psi, and lambda_l = mu_e/mu_{e-1} (ratios of the mu_n are well defined). | Working proof by injectivity of residue duality and the divisors of the boundary functions when 2c = 0; reviewed by a fresh-context referee. | [Odd generator poles](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-odd-generator-poles) |
| `lem:cube-collision-point-regularity` | On {0,1}^3 in characteristic != 2: a boundary witness P_n not containing a smooth conic through the four vertices of a coordinate plane or of the plane z1 = z2 meets it at the origin with order <= n^2 + 2n; at the non-double collision points (1:-1:0) and (1:1:2) of the line y3 = y1 + y2 the curve z(T) runs along such conics, so if W^(e) and W^(e+1) are nonzero there (equivalently P_e, P_{e+1} do not contain the conics), s = W^{P_e P_{e+1}} is nonzero and t/s is regular; P_n contains only finitely many conics of each pencil. | Working proof by Bezout on the conics and the collision-free lemma; reviewed by a fresh-context referee. | [Collision points](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-collision-points) |
| `check:cube-boundary-collision-values` | Over F_1000003, for n = 2..5 the boundary solution W^(n) (found in the S_3-trivial part) is nonzero at (1,-1,0) and (1,1,2) and zero at the double point (0,1,1); by the boundary theorem this transfers to characteristic 0 and almost every p. | Finite check by the fixed-point value mode of bmd_cube_solution_cones in series mode. | [Collision points](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-collision-points) |
| `lem:cube-line-gcd-criterion` | On {0,1}^3 in characteristic != 2, for e >= 2: if P_p lies in J^{psi(p)} (psi(p) = floor(p^2/2)) for p = e-1..e+2 and, for n = e, e+1, the gcd of the coordinates of the boundary solution W^(n) along the line y = (u, 1, u+1) of F_2 = 0 is u^{psi(n)} (and the same at u = infinity), then (W_e) holds: t/s is a quartic on each line of F_2 = 0 vanishing at the double points. | Working proof from lem:cube-odd-generator-criterion, lem:cube-odd-generator-poles, lem:cube-collision-point-regularity and lem:cube-product-cone-formula, with the order comparison psi(e-1)+psi(e+2) = psi(e)+psi(e+1)+2; reviewed by a fresh-context referee. | [Double points](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-double-points) |
| `thm:cube-odd-generators-small` | On {0,1}^3 in characteristic 0 and in characteristic p outside a finite set, (W_3) and (W_4) hold; hence every pair with 2 <= rho <= d-1 and d <= 5 rho has a free solution module with least excess B, and l_0(d+1, 4d+rho-1) = B(d, rho) for all rho >= d/5. | Working proof by lem:cube-line-gcd-criterion with its conditions checked for n <= 5 modulo 1000003 (check:cube-boundary-line-gcd) and the vertex-line theorem for P_6, transferred to characteristic 0 and almost every p, then thm:cube-peeling-reduction part 2; reviewed by a fresh-context referee. | [Double points](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-double-points) |
| `check:cube-boundary-line-gcd` | Over F_1000003, for n = 2..5: the witness space at (n,1), excess n^2-1, is one-dimensional and S_3-trivial, its jet lies in J^{psi(n)}, its cone of order psi(n) at (1:1:0) is nonzero in the direction of a line of F_2 = 0, and the gcd of the coordinates of W^(n) along y = (u,1,u+1) is u^{psi(n)} (u^2, u^4, u^8, u^12). | Finite check by bmd_cube_solution_cones (series mode, fixed cone direction, value dumps) and bmd_cube_line_gcd.py. | [Double points](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-double-points) |
| `lem:cube-residue-disc-valuation` | On {0,1}^3: let O be a complete DVR with residue characteristic != 2, K = Frac O, y in O^3, and P a polynomial with coefficients in O and h_P = T^{-k} P(z) / prod L'(z_i) nonzero, expanded at p_0 on the branch z_i = r_0(y_i T). If no zero of phi_P = T^{-k} P(z) on the curve w_i^2 = 1 + 4 y_i T over the algebraic closure lies in the residue disc of p_0 (\|T\| < 1, all w_i = 1 mod the maximal ideal), then the lowest nonzero Laurent coefficient of h_P has the least valuation among all its coefficients. | Working proof by Weierstrass preparation in O[[T]]: a smaller valuation beyond the leading term gives a distinguished factor whose root is a zero of phi_P in the disc; reviewed by a fresh-context referee. | [Residue disc](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-residue-disc) |
| `lem:cube-line-gcd-sufficiency` | On {0,1}^3, for e >= 2, in characteristic 0 or odd p with p not dividing n or p = n for n = e-1..e+2: if for n = e, e+1 the gcd of the coordinates of the boundary solution W^(n) along y = (u, 1, u+1) is u^{psi(n)}, psi(n) = floor(n^2/2), then (W_e) holds. The vertex-line hypothesis P_p in J^{psi(p)} of lem:cube-line-gcd-criterion is not needed. | Working proof: lem:cube-residue-disc-valuation on F[[u]] at the double points of the line, with the zeros of phi_n on the lines of F_2 = 0 at T = infinity or at 2-torsion points sigma_i sigma_j(p_0), and the boundary coordinate theorem; reviewed by a fresh-context referee. | [Residue disc](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-residue-disc) |
| `thm:cube-odd-generators-seven` | On {0,1}^3 in characteristic 0 and in characteristic p != 3 outside a finite set, (W_e) holds for e <= 7; hence l_0(d+1, 4d+rho-1) = B(d, rho) for every pair with 2 <= rho <= d-1 and d <= 8 rho. | Working proof by lem:cube-line-gcd-sufficiency, with the line-gcd property for n <= 5 from thm:cube-odd-generators-small and for n = 6, 7, 8 from the maximal-minor gcds of the route review modulo 1000003, made exact by lem:cube-gcd-all-m and the boundary coordinate theorem and transferred by the primitive gcd form; then thm:cube-peeling-reduction part 2 with e = 7; reviewed by a fresh-context referee. | [Residue disc](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-residue-disc) |
| `thm:cube-line-gcd-all` | On {0,1}^3, for every n >= 1, in characteristic 0 or odd p with p not dividing n or p = n: along the line y_3 = y_1 + y_2 of F_2 = 0 the coordinate W_{c_n} (c_n = 4n for odd n, 4n-1 for even n) of the primitive boundary solution W^(n) restricts to a nonzero constant times (y_1 y_2)^{psi(n)}, psi(n) = floor(n^2/2), and the gcd over F[u] of the coordinates of W^(n)(u, 1, u+1) is u^{psi(n)}; likewise on the other two lines. | Working proof by a degree count: deg W_{c_n} = 2 psi(n), order >= psi(n) at both double points of the line (boundary coordinate theorem), and W_{c_n} nonzero on the line because phi_n has pole order exactly 4n+1 or 4n there; reviewed by a fresh-context referee. | [Line-gcd proof](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-line-gcd-proof) |
| `thm:cube-torsion-partition-char-zero` | On {0,1}^3 in characteristic 0, for all 1 <= rho <= d the solution module at m = 4d+rho-1 is free and l_0(d+1, 4d+rho-1) = B(d, rho), the sum of pi_i^2 - 1 over the balanced partition of d into rho parts; in odd characteristic p outside the finite set of thm:cube-peeling-reduction, l_0 = B(d, rho) for 2 <= rho <= d-1 with d <= (2p-2) rho (freeness not claimed there). | Working proof: thm:cube-line-gcd-all and lem:cube-line-gcd-sufficiency give (W_e) for every e >= 2 in characteristic 0 (for e <= 2p-3 in characteristic p), then thm:cube-peeling-reduction parts 2 and 3; reviewed by a fresh-context referee. | [Line-gcd proof](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-line-gcd-proof) |
| `thm:cube-dimension-three-per-order` | On {0,1}^3 over a field of characteristic 0, for k >= 1, 0 <= l <= k-1 and m = k-l-1: delta(3,k,l) = 2k+1-h with h = 0 if m = 0 and otherwise h = 1 + max{d in [0, floor(m/4)] : 5d <= m+1, or 5d > m+1 and B(d, m+1-4d) <= l}, B(d,rho) = sum(pi_i^2 - 1) over the balanced partition of d into rho parts; the same holds in odd characteristic p outside the finite set of thm:cube-peeling-reduction whenever m <= 16p-12. | Working proof assembling lem:cube-threshold-ideal, thm:finite-grid-stable-law, thm:cube-dimension-three-law (kappa_3), thm:cube-order-zero-value and thm:cube-torsion-partition-char-zero; matches all 462 recorded exact kernel values over F_3, F_5, F_7 and F_101; reviewed by a fresh-context referee. | [Dimension-3 formula](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-formula) |
| `lem:cube-double-point-order-reduction` | On {0,1}^3 over every field of characteristic != 2 and for every n >= 1, every coordinate of the primitive boundary solution W^(n) vanishes to order >= floor(n^2/2) at each double point (1:1:0), (1:0:1), (0:1:1). | Working proof: characteristic 0 is thm:cube-boundary-coordinate-order part 3; in characteristic p the reduction of the primitive integral solution is a nonzero constant times the primitive solution mod p (rank-1 kernel, equal degrees), and vanishing Taylor coefficients at an integral point reduce; reviewed by a fresh-context referee. | [Odd characteristic](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-odd-characteristic) |
| `thm:cube-torsion-partition-odd` | On {0,1}^3: (W_e) holds for every e >= 2 in every odd characteristic; and in odd characteristic p outside the finite exceptional set E of thm:cube-diagonal-near-diagonal, every solution module at 1 <= rho <= d is free, l_0(d+1, 4d+rho-1) = B(d, rho), and the formula of thm:cube-dimension-three-per-order gives delta_F(3,k,l) for all k, l. | Working proof: lem:cube-double-point-order-reduction makes thm:cube-line-gcd-all and lem:cube-line-gcd-sufficiency characteristic-free; thm:cube-peeling-reduction uses the (5,2) theorem only for (W_2), so its exceptional set reduces to that of thm:cube-half-plane, which is E; reviewed by a fresh-context referee. | [Odd characteristic](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-odd-characteristic) |
| `thm:cube-diagonal-every-odd` | On {0,1}^3 over every field of characteristic != 2 the solution modules at (2,2), (3,2), (3,3) are free on generators of excesses {0,2}, {3,4}, {0,2,3}; hence the hypotheses (i)-(iii) of thm:cube-diagonal-near-diagonal hold and that theorem has no exceptional characteristic. | Working proof with an exact certificate (Macaulay2): over QQ, minimal generators whose primitive integral lifts have minor contents 150, 25, 168750 (odd primes 3, 5 only), so their reductions are bases for every other odd p by the basis criterion; over ZZ/3 and ZZ/5 the minimal generators are computed directly; reviewed by a fresh-context referee. | [Diagonal certificate](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-diagonal-certificate) |
| `thm:cube-dimension-three-every-field` | On {0,1}^3 over every field of characteristic != 2: every solution module at 1 <= rho <= d is free with l_0(d+1, 4d+rho-1) = B(d, rho), and delta_F(3,k,l) = 2k+1-h with h = 0 if m = k-l-1 = 0 and otherwise h-1 the larger of floor((m+1)/5) and the largest d <= floor(m/4) with 5d > m+1 and B(d, m+1-4d) <= l. | Working proof: thm:cube-dimension-three-per-order in characteristic 0; thm:cube-torsion-partition-odd in odd characteristic, whose exceptional set is emptied by thm:cube-diagonal-every-odd; agrees with all 918 recorded exact kernel values; reviewed by a fresh-context referee. | [Diagonal certificate](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-diagonal-certificate) |
| `lem:cube-line-threshold-bound` | On {0,1}^n over any field: if some element of I^{(h)}_m of degree l_0(h,m) does not vanish on the line y = au+bv (as for a generic line), the ideal of top coordinates of the kernel of A_m restricted to that line has initial degree <= l_0(h,m). | Working proof: substitution commutes with the linear system and keeps homogeneity and excess. | [Dimension four](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-dimension-four) |
| `check:cube-dimension-four-thresholds` | On {0,1}^4 over F_32003: l_0(3,13) = 12 (no solution of excess <= 8 at m = 13; syzygies up to excess 15 of excesses 12, 13, 14, 14, 15), line values 4, 2, 1 at m = 14, 15, 16 (lower bounds for lines outside a proper closed set); on a random line the m = 13 kernel splits as (7,7), so the global module there is not free if the line is generic; dimension-3 controls reproduce B(d,rho) globally for d = 3 and on the line for d <= 4. | Finite check by Macaulay2 graded kernels (research/tools/bmd_cube_thresholds_m2.m2), global, degree-limited and on a random line. | [Dimension four](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-dimension-four) |
| `check:cube-dimension-four-generators` | On {0,1}^4 over F_32003, the savings-3 threshold generators are: at m = 17 and 18 (l_0 = 2) scalar multiples of the S_4-invariant irreducible quadric Q = sum_{i<j} y_i y_j - 2 sum_i y_i^2; at m = 16 (l_0 = 5) three irreducible quintics; at m = 15 (l_0 = 6) one irreducible sextic. | Finite check by Macaulay2 (incremental degree-limited syzygies, factorization of top coordinates). | [Dimension-four quadric](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-dimension-four-quadric) |
| `conj:cube-dimension-four-quadric` | On {0,1}^4 in characteristic 0 and large characteristic, for every d >= 2, with M(d) the least m with l_0(d+1, m) = 0: l_0(d+1, M(d)-1) = 2, and the degree-2 part of the threshold ideal there is spanned by Q = sum_{i<j} y_i y_j - 2 sum_i y_i^2. | Conjecture from the d = 2 row over F_32003 (check:cube-dimension-four-generators), by analogy with the dimension-3 near-diagonal threshold 3 generated by the 2-torsion cubic; untested at d = 3 (the Groebner run timed out). | [Dimension-four quadric](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-dimension-four-quadric) |
| `lem:cube-symmetric-reduction` | On {0,1}^n over a field, S_n acts on the solutions of the threshold system by (sigma W)_c(y) = W_c(sigma^{-1} y), preserving excess, so I^{(h)}_m is S_n-stable; if n! is invertible, the S_n-invariant elements of I^{(h)}_m of degree l are exactly the top coordinates of the S_n-invariant solutions of excess l. | Working proof by the row-permutation identity and the Reynolds operator; reviewed by a fresh-context referee. | [Symmetric kernel](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-symmetric-kernel) |
| `check:cube-quadric-d3` | On {0,1}^4 over F_32003, savings 4 at m = 38: no invariant solution of excess 0, invariant solutions of excess 1 all with top coordinate 0, and at excess 2 the invariant top coordinates span the quadric Q = sum_{i<j} y_i y_j - 2 sum y_i^2; hence 1 <= l_0(4,38) <= 2 over F_32003 (the lower bound also in characteristic 0 and almost every p) and the invariant degree-2 part is the line of Q; the non-invariant parts in degrees 1 and 2 are untested. Controls: the 2-torsion cubic L_2 at (3,13) in dimension 3, and Q at m = 17, 18 and the threshold 6 at m = 15 in dimension 4. | Finite check by the FLINT symmetric kernel research/tools/bmd_cube_symmetric_solutions.cpp, validated on the controls. | [Symmetric kernel](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-symmetric-kernel) |
| `thm:cube-branch-point-symmetry` | On {0,1}^n over every field of characteristic != 2, every threshold ideal I^{(d+1)}_m is stable under the linear involution psi(y) = (y_1, y_1-y_2, ..., y_1-y_n), with W_m -> +-W_m o psi on homogeneous solutions of the same excess; since the ideals are homogeneous and psi = -s_{01}, they are stable under S_{n+1} permuting the branch points 0, y_1, ..., y_n (the reflection representation); <S_n, psi> = S_{n+1} x {+-1} for n >= 2. | Working proof: the Moebius substitution T -> -T/(1+4y_1T) fixes p_0, maps V_d(y) onto w_1^{-d} V_d(psi(y)) since div w_1 = H_1 - H_inf, and acts on solution windows by unimodular triangular matrices preserving the top coordinate up to sign; reviewed by a fresh-context referee. | [Branch-point symmetry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-branch-point-symmetry) |
| `cor:cube-quadric-threshold-d3` | On {0,1}^4 over F_32003: l_0(4,38) = 2 and l_0(3,17) = l_0(3,18) = 2; the degree-2 part of the threshold ideal there is the line of Q = sum_{i<j} y_i y_j - 2 sum y_i^2 plus possibly a [3,2] component of S_5. | Working proof from thm:cube-branch-point-symmetry and the S_4-invariant computations of check:cube-quadric-d3 (I_1 is 0 or all of the irreducible reflection representation, and has no S_4-invariant element). | [Branch-point symmetry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-branch-point-symmetry) |
| `lem:cube-generic-normality` | For every n >= 1 and every degree vector (nu_r)_{r in {0,1}^n} with nu_r >= -1, the determinant Delta_nu(a) of the coefficients of T^0..T^{N-1} in T^j w^r (j <= nu_r, w_i = (1+a_iT)^{1/2}, N = sum(nu_r+1)) is a nonzero polynomial over Z[1/2]: in characteristic 0 every multi-index is normal for the system {w^r} at generic centres, and for fixed nu the same holds in odd characteristic outside a finite set of primes. | Working proof: the Wronskian of T^j w^r on the curve w_i^2 = 1+a_iT is nonzero in characteristic 0, and the transport to a general point q gives Delta_nu(a/(1+aT(q))) != 0. | [Exact collision exponents](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-collision-exponents-exact) |
| `thm:cube-boundary-collision-exponents` | On {0,1}^n in characteristic 0, n >= 2, d >= 1, N = N_{2,n}(d) and every m >= N-1: along each collision divisor y_i = 0 or y_i = y_j the nonzero elementary divisors of the N x (m+1) constraint matrix are exactly the d - e(P), so the gcd g_{n,d} of the boundary minors and Delta_{n,d} both have exponent E_n(d) = sum_k C(n-1,k) floor((d-k+1)^2/4) there; hence l_0(d+1,N) = deg Delta_{n,d} - C(n+1,2) E_n(d) - deg g^nc, which on {0,1}^4 (d >= 2) is 10d^2 - 10d - 5 - deg g^nc_{4,d}, with g^nc the part of g prime to the collision forms. For fixed (n,d) the exponents hold in odd characteristic outside finitely many primes. | Working proof: the collision limit lemma's basis of the saturation, normality of its limit space from lem:cube-generic-normality, saturation at every truncation m >= N-1, and the Moebius transport; the closed forms are asserted by research/tools/bmd_cube_collision_counts.py. | [Exact collision exponents](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-collision-exponents-exact) |
| `prop:cube-extra-factors-double` | On {0,1}^n in characteristic 0 (n >= 2, d >= 1), every prime factor of the boundary gcd g_{n,d} other than the collision forms divides Delta_{n,d} at least twice; hence if the non-collision part of Delta_{n,d} is squarefree, l_0(d+1, N_{2,n}(d)) = deg Delta_{n,d} - C(n+1,2) E_n(d), which is 10d^2 - 10d - 5 on {0,1}^4 for d >= 2. | Working proof: at a general point of such a factor, p_0 has top order >= N+1 and so weight >= 2; the Wronskian's order at p_0 equals the order in t of Delta along the transport curve a/(1+at), which is transversal to the factor because it is not invariant under the flow of sum a_i^2 d/da_i. | [Exact collision exponents](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-collision-exponents-exact) |

| `lem:cube-quadrangle-diagonal` | Over a field of characteristic 0 (or p not dividing 2 mu), no form of degree mu >= 1 on P^2 restricts on each of the six sides of a complete quadrangle to a nonzero multiple of the mu-th power of the linear form vanishing at that side's diagonal point: if each restriction is kappa_ij times that power, all kappa_ij = 0. | Working proof by coordinates A_i = coordinate points and (1:1:1), and a two-coefficient comparison on the side x = z; checked for mu <= 7 by exact linear algebra. | [Squarefree reduction](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-squarefree-reduction) |
| `lem:cube-no-double-double-surface` | For n >= 3 in characteristic 0, no homogeneous polynomial of positive degree in y_1..y_n restricts on every collision hyperplane D_ab = {r_a = r_b} to a nonzero constant times a product of double-double forms r_z - r_w ({z,w} disjoint from {a,b}). | Working proof: the lowest part of the local expansion at a general point of a quadruple stratum through a double-double factor (so the order is >= 1), restricted to a transverse 3-space, contradicts lem:cube-quadrangle-diagonal. | [Squarefree reduction](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-squarefree-reduction) |
| `thm:cube-squarefree-reduction` | In characteristic 0, n >= 4, d >= 1: Delta_U = c prod_{j>=2} y_j^{2E_n(d)} prod_{2<=i<j} (y_i-y_j)^{E_n(d)} Delta^nc_{n,d}\|_{y_1=0} for the collision limit space U^{(n-1)}_d; and if Delta_U has multiplicity exactly 2E_n(d) along each y_j and a squarefree part prime to the collision forms of y_2..y_n, then Delta^nc_{n,d} is squarefree, g_{n,d} = c' prod l_D^{E_n(d)} and l_0(d+1, N) = deg Delta_{n,d} - C(n+1,2) E_n(d) (10d^2 - 10d - 5 for n = 4). | Working proof from the collision lifts and limit lemmas, thm:cube-boundary-collision-exponents, the S_{n+1} transport, lem:cube-no-double-double-surface and prop:cube-extra-factors-double. | [Squarefree reduction](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-squarefree-reduction) |

| `lem:cube-confluence-valuation` | In characteristic 0, for every n >= 1 and degree vector nu on {0,1}^n (alpha_{r'} = nu_{(r',0)}, beta_{r'} = nu_{(r',1)}), a_n^{e(nu)} with e(nu) = sum_{r'} (alpha_{r'}+1)(beta_{r'}+1) exactly divides the Hermite-Pade determinant Delta_nu of {T^j w^r}, and (Delta_nu / a_n^{e(nu)}) at a_n = 0 is a nonzero rational multiple of Delta_{nu'}(a_1..a_{n-1}) with nu'_{r'} = alpha_{r'} + beta_{r'} + 1; the one-variable systems {A + B(1+U)^{1/2}} are normal for all degree pairs. | Working proof: one-variable normality by a first-order differential elimination, then a row change to the order-adapted basis f_k(a_n T) of each block and the binomial identity C(a+b+2,2) - C(a+1,2) - C(b+1,2) = (a+1)(b+1). | [Confluence](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-confluence) |

| `lem:cube-first-step-sandwich` | Over any field, for all n, d >= 1 and every point y*, the zero set of the first-step threshold ideal I = I^{(d+1)}_{N+1} satisfies {rank A_N < N, rank A_{N+1} = N} subset V(I) subset {rank A_N < N}. | Working proof: I = (Im A_N : a), which is the unit ideal locally where A_N has full rank; and where rank A_N < N but rank A_{N+1} = N the two-dimensional kernel of A_{N+1}(y*) consists of padded kernel vectors of A_N(y*), whose last coordinate is 0. | [First-step sandwich](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-first-step-sandwich) |

| `thm:cube-collision-regime-torsion` | On {0,1}^4 in characteristic != 2 with d >= 2: at a point (0, y') of a collision hyperplane with y' distinct nonzero, the threshold ideal I^{(d+1)}_m is the unit ideal unless the collision limit space U_d(y') has an element of order >= m; since U_d(y') lies in L(2d H_inf) on the genus-1 limit curve, this never happens for m >= 8d+1, and at m = 8d only where 2d [H_inf - 4 p_0] = 0; so for m >= 8d+1 the zero sets of the threshold ideals lie in the 25 lines where collision hyperplanes meet. | Working proof: the polynomial factorization A = S Delta_1 A^Lambda from the collision lifts, the limit rows at y_1 = 0, the degree bound on the genus-1 curve, S_5 symmetry and thm:cube-threshold-collision-support. | [Collision regime](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-collision-regime) |

| `lem:cube-isotypic-detection` | On {0,1}^n in characteristic 0 or p > n+1, for nu a partition of n, mu = nu with a part 1 added, and e >= 0: if every lambda of n+1 with n(lambda) = sum (i-1) lambda_i <= e dominates mu, then the degree-e part of I^{(h)}_m is nonzero iff some S_nu-invariant solution of excess e has nonzero top coordinate; so S_n-invariant solutions decide l_0 <= 1 for every n, and for n = 4 S_3-, S_2 x S_2- and S_2-invariant solutions decide every e <= 3, 5, 9. | Working proof: S_{n+1}-stability of I_m, Chevalley's decomposition with fake degrees (U_lambda first occurs in degree n(lambda)), Young's rule, and Reynolds averaging over S_nu. | [Invariant thresholds](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-invariant-thresholds) |

| `lem:cube-boundary-generator-invariant` | On {0,1}^3 in characteristic != 2, for every d >= 1 the generator D_d = Delta_{3,d}/g_{3,d} of the principal boundary threshold ideal I^{(d+1)}_{4d} is S_4-invariant and vanishes identically on no collision line. | Working proof: I_N principal (rank-1 reflexive), so D_d is a semi-invariant; a sign-type semi-invariant vanishes on every mirror; by the collision lifts, D_d is nonzero at a general point of y_3 = 0 because the genus-0 collision limit U_d misses the order-4d function psi^(2d), whose w_1 w_2 T^(d-1) coefficient is a nonzero polynomial (Lucas). | [Invariant thresholds in dimension 3](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-invariant-dimension-three) |
| `thm:cube-invariant-attainment-dimension-three` | On {0,1}^3 in characteristic != 2, whenever I^{(d+1)}_m != 0 its initial degree l_0 is attained by an S_4-invariant form, a nonzero multiple of prod_i D_{p_i} (balanced partition of the dimension-3 law); in characteristic != 2, 3 also l_0 = l_0^{S_3}; this is conj:cube-invariant-attainment for n = 3. | Working proof from lem:cube-boundary-generator-invariant, the product bound's lowest parts, the dimension-3 law and Reynolds averaging. | [Invariant thresholds in dimension 3](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-invariant-dimension-three) |
| `thm:cube-boundary-generator-invariant-all-n` | On {0,1}^n in characteristic 0, for every n >= 2 and d >= 1, the boundary threshold ideal I^{(d+1)}_N (N = N_{2,n}(d)) is principal, generated by W_N = Delta_{n,d}/g_{n,d} = c Delta^nc/g^nc, which is S_{n+1}-invariant and vanishes on no collision hyperplane; so l_0 at every boundary is attained by an invariant, and Delta^nc, g^nc are invariants too. | Working proof: rank-1 reflexive kernel, semi-invariance under the S_{n+1}-stable principal ideal, a sign-type semi-invariant vanishes on every mirror, and v_D(W_N) = v_D(Delta) - v_D(g) = 0 for every collision D (collision-exponent theorem). | [Boundary generator invariant](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-boundary-invariant) |

| `thm:cube-order-zero-dimension-four-linear-bound` | On {0,1}^4 in characteristic 0 (and every odd characteristic except 5, 179, 281, 2959174039205819), the order-zero threshold M(d) (least m = k-1 with savings >= d+1 at origin order 0) satisfies M(d) <= 20d - 21 for every d >= 2, with M(1) = 5 and M(2) = 19 exactly in characteristic 0: products give M(d1+d2-1) <= M(d1) + M(d2) + 1, and an exact rational certificate gives M(2) <= 19. | Working proof: the product rule at origin order 0 and an exact rational solution of the symmetric order-zero system at d = 2, m = 19 (research/tools/bmd_cube_order_zero_exact.cpp, verified A x = b over Z), with exact unsolvability for m <= 18. | [Order zero is at most 20d - 21](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-order-zero-linear) |
| `ex:cube-order-zero-quadratic-false` | conj:cube-order-zero-dimension-four-quadratic (M(d) = 3d^2 + 5d - 3 on {0,1}^4 in characteristic 0) is false for every d >= 4, in characteristic 0 and in large odd characteristic: M(d) <= 20d - 21 < 3d^2 + 5d - 3, e.g. M(4) <= 59 < 65. | Refutation from thm:cube-order-zero-dimension-four-linear-bound; 3d^2 + 5d - 3 - (20d - 21) = 3(d-2)(d-3) > 0 for d >= 4. | [Order zero is at most 20d - 21](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-order-zero-linear) |

| `thm:cube-order-zero-rate` | On {0,1}^n over every field, with b_n(e) the least multiplicity k with savings >= e+n-2 at origin order 0: b_n is subadditive and nondecreasing, b_n(e) >= 2^{n-1} e, and if one b_n(e_0) is finite the limit c_n = lim b_n(e)/e = inf b_n(e)/e exists (Fekete), and the savings at every k are k/c_n + O(1) from above and k/c_n - o(k) from below; c_1 = 1, c_2 = 2, c_3 = 5 (characteristic != 2), 8 <= c_4 <= 20 (characteristic 0 and odd characteristic outside 5, 179, 281, 2959174039205819), and c_n = 2^{n-1} in characteristic 2. | Working proof: the product rule at origin order 0 (savings h_1 + h_2 - n + 2), the multiplicity Schwartz-Zippel bound, Fekete's lemma; values from the recorded per-order laws and the linear order-zero bound. | [Order-zero rate](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-order-zero-rate) |
| `lem:cube-triple-double-windows` | On {0,1}^4 in characteristic != 2, d >= 2, at the triple-double point P = (0,0,c,c) (c != 0), every solution W of the (d+1)-system satisfies: W(P) kills w^i, w = (1+4cT)^{1/2}, for -(4d-5) <= i <= 7d-7 and i = 4d (11d - 11 exponents for d >= 3, [-3, 8] for d = 2). | Working proof adapting lem:cube-double-point-windows: restriction to y_1 = 0, lifts along y_2 -> 0, the arc y_3 -> y_4 (window [-(4d-5), 4d-2] and 4d), and the Mobius transport to the frame with the pair at infinity (window [-(6d-7), 2d], transported to [-d, 7d-7]). | [Triple-double windows](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-triple-double-windows) |

| `lem:uniform-prefix-vacuity` | Uniform-prefix vacuity: over F_3, for a W_RS block with forms L_1..L_h, zero-pattern map g(x) in {0,1}^h and prefix matrix C uniform in F_3^{t x h} (clauses g_i Q^C, Q^C = [Cg = 0]), the allowed set is {x : g(x) not in K_C} with K_C = {g != 0 : Cg = 0}; each nonzero pattern is killed with probability 3^{-t}, so the block is vacuous with probability >= 1 - (2^h - 1) 3^{-t}, and c independent copies kill a given pattern with probability <= c 3^{-t}; with t = (K+1) log_3 n + O(log log n), all M <= n^K blocks kill a given pattern with probability O(1/n). | `prop:local-design-criterion` | Local design criterion: for a finite point set B, a subspace Lambda of functions (e.g. the row terms x_T(r_i - 1)) and clause sets S with allowed sets P_S in B, the constant 1 lies outside Lambda_{<=D} + sum_S I(P_S)_{<=D} iff there is a functional mu on functions of degree <= D with mu(1) = 1, mu(Lambda) = 0 and, for every S, a measure on P_S agreeing with mu in degree <= D (a local design); a local design is a degree-D Nullstellensatz dual functional for Lambda, the clauses and all closed members; a design supported on the whole allowed set (prop:failure-set-criterion) is local; conj:satisfiable-cover-generation implies local designs exist, in the setting stated in the entry. | Working proof (linear duality) after a fresh-context review. | [Local design criterion](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-28-local-design-criterion) |

For a vanishing quadratic section s=c0+c1 z+sum c_ij w_ij, its branch normal covector is b_i=1/2 sum_(j!=i)c_ij [w_ij f]_+(a_i), and its quadratic differential equals Tr(eta_f ds). (1) A nonzero section vanishes to order >=L+3 at P iff rank A_L(a)<R. (2) ord_{s=0}F_sep(e^{s delta}a)=wt_P(a) for delta=-sum a_i^2 d/da_i, so wt_P>=m iff F_sep,...,delta^{m-1}F_sep vanish at a. (3) The vanishing order of z->F_sep(1/(a_i-z)) at a finite non-branch z0 is the ramification weight over the corresponding fibre. (4) delta F_sep=(3/2)(N-1)(sum a_i)F_sep+R m_{R-1}, and where rank A_{R-2}=R-1 the ideal I_R(A_R) equals (F_sep, delta F_sep) locally. | Working proof passed by one fresh-context medium reviewer. | `thm:cube-wronskian-discriminant-criterion` | Characteristic zero, N>=3. Corollary: if P = F(t^N - s) on a closed annulus K with F, s zero-free, \|t s'/s\| < N on K, \|s\| < r2^N on the outer and \|s\| > r1^N on the inner circle, then P has exactly N - wind(s) zeros in K, all simple. | Working proof: direct differentiation at a zero and the argument principle. | [Log-derivative criterion](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-03-cube-far-logderivative-criterion) |
| `conj:cube-last-far-coefficient-cut-blocks` | Hypothesis (refuted): on each long Newton edge [m1, m2] of P(t) = (1-t)^d W_(b-1)(t/(1-t)), the mid-edge cut A = P mod t^c, B = P div t^c (c = floor((m1+m2)/2)) satisfies (sup\|tA'/A - m1\| + sup\|tB'/B - (m2-c)\|)/(m2-m1) < 1 on the band \|log\|t\| - log r\| <= pi/L, which with lem:far-logderivative-criterion would make all roots on the circle simple. | Refuted at e = 4..11: the ratio is between 1.86 and 15.3 on all 96 tested circles, not decreasing in e (research/tools/bmd_cube_last_far_block_logderiv.gp, research/results/bmd-20261003-zzp/block-logderiv-2.txt). | [Log-derivative criterion](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-03-cube-far-logderivative-criterion) |
| `conj:cube-last-far-log-radii` | For every e, the slopes -u_0 > ... > -u_3 of the four long Newton edges of P(t) = (1-t)^d W_(b-1)(t/(1-t)) satisfy N u_i = c_i log N + d_i + o(1) (N = R_e + 7/2) with equal consecutive differences c_(i+1) - c_i: the far-root circles lie at distance Theta(log N/N) from \|t\| = 1, with log-radii in arithmetic progression of step about 4.1 log N/N. | Conjecture: at e = 4..11 the fits N u_i = c_i log N + d_i have c ~ (-6.72, -2.65, 1.52, 5.61) (with a 1/e term: -6.72, -2.55, 1.52, 5.71) and residuals <= 0.021, while e u = C + D/e, N u = a sqrt(e) + b and a N^(1/4) + b fit far worse (research/tools/bmd_cube_last_far_log_radii.py, research/results/bmd-20261003-zzq/log-radii.txt); equal differences hold to about +-0.1. | [Last far log radii](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-03-cube-last-far-log-radii) |
| `conj:cube-last-far-radius-step` | For every e, the four far-root circles of the last even-peeling step satisfy N u_i = (4i - 13/2) log N + O(1), so N(u_(i+1) - u_i) = 4 log N + O(1) (N = R_e + 7/2; -u_i the long-edge slopes of P(t) = (1-t)^d W_(b-1)(t/(1-t))), as a leading-order count of the multilinear expansion over the block-IV splitting predicts (exponent (21 - 8m)/2 of T_m/T_(m-1) in units of log N). | Conjecture with a heuristic derivation (next-order corrections of relative size about k^2/n ~ 8 uncontrolled): at e = 4..11, N du - 4 log N = const + f/e fits with residuals <= 0.032 against 0.05-0.10 for slopes 3.5, 4.5, and N u_i - (4i - 13/2) log N = d + f/e fits best on every circle (residuals <= 0.037) against slopes shifted by 1/2 (research/tools/bmd_cube_last_far_radius_exponents.py, research/results/bmd-20261003-zzr/radius-exponents.txt). | [Last far radius step](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-03-cube-last-far-radius-step) |
| `lem:two-block-wronskian` | For a not an integer and all p, q >= 1: W(x^a P_<p + (1+x)^a P_<q) = c x^(pa-pq) (1+x)^(qa-pq) R(x) with R polynomial, R(0) = 1, R(-1) != 0, deg R = min(p,q)\|p-q\|, and c = +- sf(p) sf(q) prod_(i<p, j<q) (a+i-j), sf(m) = prod_(i<m) i!; for p = q the Wronskian is c (x(1+x))^(p(a-p)) with no far zeros. | Working proof by local exponents at 0, -1, infinity (Taylor minor det[binom(a+i,j)] = 1, tail minor via det[1/(i+s)!] = +- sf(q)/prod (i+q)!), the degree count and the involution x -> -1-x; exact strict check of 150 cases, p, q <= 5, six values of a (research/tools/bmd_cube_two_block_closed_form.gp, research/results/bmd-20261003-zzt/two-block-closed-form.txt). | [Two block Wronskian](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-03-cube-two-block-wronskian) |
| `lem:block-pair-wronskian` | For classes c with a_c pairwise incongruent mod Z, each a_c non-integral or an integer <= -max(p_c,q_c): W(sum_c x^(a_c) P_<p_c + (1+x)^(a_c) P_<q_c) = C x^alpha (1+x)^beta R(x), R polynomial with R(0) = 1, R(-1) != 0, deg R = PQ - sum_c min(p_c,q_c)^2 (P = sum p_c, Q = sum q_c), alpha = sum (p_c a_c + binom(p_c,2)) + binom(Q,2) - binom(K,2), \|C\| = \|V(mu_0)\| \|V(y)\|/sf(Q). | Working proof by local exponents (joint Taylor minor V(y)/sf(Q), per-class tail minors via Gamma factors and det[1/(i+s)!], the involution for p_c < q_c) and the degree count; exact check of 2197 multi-class cases, 80 with the integral class -n-3 and 135 at the boundary a_c = -max(p_c,q_c) (research/tools/bmd_cube_block_pair_wronskian.gp, research/results/bmd-20261003-zzu/block-pair.txt). | [Block pair Wronskian](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-03-cube-block-pair-wronskian) |
| `conj:cube-last-far-ideal-balance` | Hypothesis (refuted as a description at e = 4..6): at every size e the far circles of the last step are the balance circles mean_\|t\|=r log\|T_(i+1)/T_i\| = 0 of the idealized block-IV expansion terms T_m = A_m Pi_m W_m (4x4 Laplace amplitude, residual Pochhammers, two-class monomial Wronskian of lem:block-pair-wronskian, echelon residuals replaced by leading monomials). | Refuted as a description at e = 4..6: on circle 2 the predicted u N/log N misses the hull value by 3.9, 3.3, 2.9 and on circle 0 by 2.3, 1.6, 1.2, stable under a 150/400-digit control at e = 4 (circle 1 secant convergence unverified); asymptotics untested; no code bug found by the reviewer (research/tools/bmd_cube_last_far_ideal_terms.gp, research/results/bmd-20261003-zzv/). | [Last far ideal balance](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-03-cube-last-far-ideal-balance) |
| `conj:cube-last-far-split-balance` | Hypothesis (refuted at e = 4, 5, 6): splitting each block-IV image after d_x^n by t-degree (cut c near n/2 or n/3) and pushing both parts through the six-space operators gives exact terms T_m (sum_m T_m = W_t of the six-space) of which T_i, T_(i+1) dominate and balance on the i-th far circle (i = 0..3) of the last step. | Refuted: sum_m T_m = W_t holds exactly, but on every circle, size and cut the largest circle-mean term is T_2 (T_1 or T_3 second), and the pair T_i, T_(i+1) of circle i has no balance within 0.6 in log r (grid step 0.05), windows that for the pairs with T_2 cover all four circles (research/tools/bmd_cube_last_far_split_terms.gp, research/results/bmd-20261003-zzw/split-terms.txt). | [Last far split balance](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-03-cube-last-far-split-balance) |
| `lem:cube-last-far-frobenius-shift` | For every e and odd prime p > d = R_(e+2), q = (p-1)/2: W_(F_p)(V_p) = (x^3(1+x)^3)^d prod kappa_i^(-1) (W(F_(b-1)) mod p), V_p = x^3(1+x)^3 P_<n + x^3 + (1+x)^3 + x^3(1+x)^q P_<4e + x^q(1+x)^3 P_<4e + x^q(1+x)^(q+1) P_<4 (half-integral exponents shifted by p/2); so (W(F) = C x^alpha (1+x)^beta W_(b-1), W_(b-1) primitive, v_p(C) >= 0) W(V_p) = 0 iff v_p(C) > 0, and otherwise the far parts of W(V_p) and W_(b-1) mod p are proportional. | Working proof: x^(p/2), (1+x)^(p/2) are constants in characteristic p and the Wronskian is multilinear; exact check at e = 1, 2, 3 (14 primes above the window proportional with full degree; window primes below 2n+8e+7 give W(V_p) = 0; p = 2n+8e+7 = 17, 61 proportional) (research/tools/bmd_cube_last_far_frobenius_shift.gp, research/results/bmd-20261003-zzy/frobenius-shift.txt). | [Last far Frobenius shift](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-03-cube-last-far-frobenius-shift) |
| `lem:cube-last-far-pivot-minors` | For every e (n = R_e, k = 4e, C = {-3} u {-7/2+j : j < k}): the integral pivot minors at 0 and -1 of prop:cube-last-far-eisenstein-branch have \|.\| = \|V(C)\| prod_(c in C) \|c^(falling n)\| / prod_(i<=k) (n+i)!, and the half-integral minor at -1 has \|.\| = 12 prod_(j<4) \|(j-7/2)^(falling k-1)\| / prod_(i<4) (k-1+i)!; all are nonzero (so I_(-1) = I_0, H_(-1) = H_0) and all six pivot minors (with lem:cube-last-far-eisenstein-minors) are p-adic units at every window prime p > 2n+5; a window prime divides the integral minors exactly when it is 2n+1, 2n+3 or 2n+5. | Working proof by falling-factorial factorization to Vandermonde determinants; exact check e = 1..8 against direct determinants, with window primes dividing the integral minors exactly 2n+1, 2n+3, 2n+5 when prime (137 at e = 6, 241 at e = 8) (research/tools/bmd_cube_last_far_pivot_minors.gp, research/results/bmd-20261003-zzz/pivot-minors.txt). | [Last far pivot minors](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-03-cube-last-far-pivot-minors) |
| `conj:cube-last-far-leading-coefficient` | For every e, every prime factor of lc(W_(b-1)) (primitive in Z[x]) is at most 8e+7 < d; equivalently, with lc = +- L_infinity / C (W(F) = C x^alpha (1+x)^beta W_(b-1)), v_q(C) = v_q(L_infinity) for every prime q > 8e+7. Then no window prime divides lc and prop:cube-last-far-eisenstein-branch holds unconditionally at window primes above max(d, 2n+5). | Conjecture: largest prime of \|lc\| is 7, 17, 19, 31, 47, 47, 53, 61, 79, 79, 89 at e = 1..11 against 8e+7 (equality at e = 5, 9); v_p(W(0)) = v_p(W(-1)) = 1 at every window prime above 2n+5 for e <= 11 (research/tools/bmd_cube_last_far_leading_coefficient.gp, research/results/bmd-20261004-a/leading-coefficient.txt). | [Last far leading coefficient](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-last-far-leading-coefficient) |
| `conj:cube-last-far-gp-structured` | Hypothesis (refuted at e = 4..8): at window primes max(d, 2n+5) < p <= 2n+8e+7 the non-branch factor G_p of W_(b-1) mod p factors over F_p into pieces of a regular (hypergeometric-type) degree pattern, unlike a random polynomial of its degree. | Refuted: at 46 window primes G_p (degree 114-536) has 4-11 irreducible factors (random expectation 5.3-6.9) with largest factor 0.27-0.98 of the degree, like the 26 no-collapse control primes (3-10 factors, 0.31-0.98) (research/tools/bmd_cube_last_far_gp_factor_degrees.gp, research/results/bmd-20261004-c/gp-factor-degrees.txt). | [Last far G_p random](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-last-far-gp-random) |
| `lem:cube-base-deformation-splitting` | If W_s(z) is jointly holomorphic and z0 is a root of W_0 of multiplicity m with d_s W(z0) != 0, the m roots near z0 are simple for small s != 0 (Rouche). Hence (B) at N (N >= 5) holds if some interior configuration D0 attaining T(b), with holomorphic non-branch part W_D (constant branch exponents and degree), has no root at a branch value and, for every root of multiplicity >= 3 of W_(D0), some configuration derivative d_v W(z0) != 0. | Working proof: rescaling with Rouche and Hurwitz near each root, a common direction outside finitely many hyperplanes, multiplicity <= 2 preserved, no roots from infinity, openness of attainment (cited); analogous to lem:cube-far-first-order-splitting at interior configurations. | [Base deformation splitting](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-base-deformation-splitting) |
| `conj:cube-middle-far-ore-separable` | For every even-peeling middle step 2 <= k <= b-2 there is a collapse prime p with v_p(W_k(0)) = 1, all residual polynomials of the Newton polygon of W_k(y-1) at p separable (observed: a staircase of height-1 sides with lengths mostly increasing by 2), and non-branch multiplicity <= 2; by Dumas and Ore this certifies that W_k has roots of multiplicity <= 2. | Conjecture: at l = 2 ((b,k) = (6,4), (7,5), (8,6)) all 37 collapse primes have separable residual polynomials at -1 (6-8 sides, as many as v_p(W(-1)); two sides of height 2) (research/tools/bmd_cube_middle_far_ore.gp, research/results/bmd-20261004-f/middle-ore.txt). | [Middle far Ore staircase](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-middle-far-ore-staircase) |
| `conj:cube-middle-far-branch-count` | For every middle even-peeling step (l >= 2) and primes p in an upper window of the collapse range, the pivot minors at 0, -1, infinity are p-adic units, v_p(W_k(0)/lc) = 1 and v_p(W_k(-1)/lc) = c(l) (c(2) = 6), both arising only from Vandermonde pairs of local exponents at distance p/2. | Conjecture: \|W(0)/lc\| = \|L_0/L_oo\| and \|W(-1)/lc\| = \|L_-1/L_oo\| hold exactly at (b,k) = (6,4), (7,5), (8,6); at the upper collapse primes (61..83, 97..127, 137..173) minors are units and the valuations are 1 and 6 from Vandermonde pairs; lower primes have p in the minors (research/tools/bmd_cube_middle_far_branch_values.gp, research/results/bmd-20261004-g/middle-branch-values.txt). | [Middle far branch count](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-middle-far-branch-count) |
| `conj:cube-far-layer-count` | For every even-peeling step (e, l) with e large enough relative to l, there is a run of primes p just above d = R_e+1+R_l+4e+4l+4el at which all pivot minors at 0, -1, infinity are p-adic units, v_p(L_0/L_oo) = 1 and v_p(L_-1/L_oo) = R_l = l(2l-1); hence v_p(W_k(0)/lc) = 1 and v_p(W_k(-1)/lc) = R_l. | Conjecture: holds at (e,l) = (3,1) p = 47..61, (3,2) 67..83, (3,3) 97..109, (4,3) 137..157 with unit minors; at (2,4) no run above d (valuations <= 18 < 28) (research/tools/bmd_cube_middle_far_branch_values.gp scan mode, research/results/bmd-20261004-h/layer-scan.txt). | [Far layer count](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-far-layer-count) |
| `lem:cube-far-layer-count` | For every even-peeling step (e, l) with the generic local exponent sets (E) of its far component (I_0 = [-R_l-2,-3] u [0,R_e+4e], H_0 = [4e-4el-7/2, 4e+4l-9/2], I_-1 = {-3} u [0,M-1], H_-1 = -7/2+[0,4e+4l-1], I_oo = [-(R_e-1),0] u [3,R_l+4l+3], H_oo = 9/2-4e+[0,4el+4e-1], M = R_e+R_l+4el) and every prime p > d with Q_lo = max(M+3-4e-4l, 4el+3, R_l+4l+4e-1) <= (p-1)/2 <= R_e+4el+3: N_0 - N_oo = 1 and N_-1 - N_oo = R_l, so with unit pivot minors and p not dividing lc, v_p(W_k(0)) = 1 (Eisenstein cluster at 0) and v_p(W_k(-1)) = R_l. | Working proof by interval counting (Step 2 of the Eisenstein proposition generalized); (E) checked exactly at seven (e, l) and the window matches all scanned valuations (research/tools/bmd_cube_middle_far_branch_values.gp sets and scan modes, research/results/bmd-20261004-i/exponent-sets.txt, research/results/bmd-20261004-h/layer-scan.txt). | [Far layer count lemma](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-far-layer-count-lemma) |
| `lem:cube-far-pivot-minors` | For every even-peeling step (e, l) the six pivot minors of the far component at 0, -1, infinity are, in absolute value, beta(C,s) = \|V(C)\| prod \|c^(falling s)\| / prod (s+i)! for explicit sets C (integral at 0: {-3} u {-7/2+j}_(j<4e), s = R_e; half at -1: {1/2-4l+j}_(j<4l), s = 4e-1; integral at oo: {-3} u {-5/2+j}_(j<4l), s = R_l; half at oo: {-7/2+j}_(j<4e), s = 4el), \|V(C_-1)\| / prod_(i<M) i! (integral at -1), and the box product prod_(i<4l) \|binom(-5/2+i, s)\| / binom(s+i, s), s = 4e+4l-4 (half at 0); all are nonzero, so the exponent sets (E) of lem:cube-far-layer-count hold. In its window all six are p-adic units for l >= 3 and for l = 2, e <= 2; for l = 2, e >= 3 only the integral minor at -1 can fail, with valuation 2 at p = 4e^2+6e+3 and 1 at p = 4e^2+6e+5. | Working proof by unitriangular reduction to two determinant identities (falling-factorial Vandermonde and the box formula) and prime bounds; exact checks of all six forms at twelve (e, l) and the predicted exceptions 241 (valuation 2), 383 and 653 (research/tools/bmd_cube_middle_far_branch_values.gp minors mode, research/results/bmd-20261004-j/). | [Far pivot minors](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-far-pivot-minors) |
| `cor:cube-far-branch-valuations` | For every even-peeling step (e, l) and every prime p > d with Q_lo <= (p-1)/2 <= R_e+4el+3 (the window of lem:cube-far-layer-count) and p not dividing lc(W_k), excluding p in {2R_e+1, 2R_e+3, 2R_e+5} when l = 1: v_p(W_k(0)) = 1 (Eisenstein cluster at 0); if moreover p is not 4e^2+6e+3 or 4e^2+6e+5 when l = 2, then v_p(W_k(-1)) = R_l. | Working proof: lem:cube-far-pivot-minors supplies (E) and unit minors for lem:cube-far-layer-count. | [Far pivot minors](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-far-pivot-minors) |
| `lem:cube-far-chain-reduction` | For an even-peeling far step (e, l), normalized c = 1, and m = R_l, let T_j be the non-branch part of the far Wronskian with A-block exponents -(j+2)..-3 and the other classes unchanged (so T_m = W_k), and Q_A the swapped Wronskian of lem:cube-far-first-order-splitting. Crum's identity gives T_(m-1) T_(m+1) = const x^s (1+x)^t [x(1+x)(T_m Q_A' - T_m' Q_A) + ((a_Q-a_m)(1+x) + (c_Q-c_m)x) T_m Q_A] (s, t integers), so gcd(T_m, T_(m-1) T_(m+1)) = 1 implies gcd(W_k, Q_A) = 1; if moreover G_A is linearly independent of G_B, G_C as functions of D, the first-order criterion holds at every multiple root of W_k. | Working proof from Crum's Wronskian identity and lem:cube-far-first-order-splitting; identity checked exactly modulo 2^61-1 at (e,l) = (1,2),(2,2),(1,3),(3,2),(2,3) (research/tools/bmd_cube_far_chain_coprime.gp, research/results/bmd-20261004-k/chain-coprime.txt). | [Far chain review](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-far-chain-review) |
| `conj:cube-far-chain-coprime` | For every even-peeling step (e, l) with l >= 2 and m = R_l, the A-chain Wronskian T_m (= W_k) is coprime to T_(m-1) and to T_(m+1). | Conjecture: all gcds trivial modulo 2^61-1 at (e,l) = (1,2),(2,2),(1,3),(3,2),(2,3); no three-term recurrence, Adler-Moser-type companion identity or resultant product formula found (research/results/bmd-20261004-k/chain-coprime.txt, chain-tests.txt). | [Far chain review](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-far-chain-review) |
| `lem:cube-far-derivative-ladder` | For an even-peeling far step (e, l), c = 1, y = 1/x and Psi = y^-3 U (U the non-A classes, dim k), m >= 2: dim Psi^(j) = k for all j (monodromy), and off {0,-1,inf}, T_j has the roots of Wr_y(Psi^(j)) (j >= 1) and Q_A those of Wr_y(y, Psi^(m-1)); at a root r of T_m with T_(m-1)(r) != 0, mult_r T_m = ord_r(f_0 - 1) - k and Q_A(r) = 0 iff f_1^(k)(r) = 0 (adapted basis of Psi^(m-1)); if moreover mult_r T_m >= 3 and Q_A(r) = 0 then mult_r T_(m+1) >= 3. Hence (with independent G's, l >= 2) the first-order criterion fails at r only if T_(m-1)(r) = 0 or r is a root of multiplicity >= 3 of both T_m and T_(m+1). | Working proof by the derivative identity Wr(1..y^(j-1), g) = prod i! Wr(g^(j)), adapted bases and weights; y-side control at nine (e, l, m) (research/tools/bmd_cube_far_chain_coprime.gp ladder mode, research/results/bmd-20261004-l/ladder.txt). | [Far derivative ladder](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-far-derivative-ladder) |
| `lem:cube-far-ga-asymmetry` | In the first-order splitting of the even peeling (l >= 2, w_s = 1/D_s): each G_X depends only on the span of class X, so G_B and G_C are symmetric in w; if G_A is not invariant under some permutation of the w_s then G_A is not in span(G_B, G_C) and the first-order criterion holds at every root r of W_k with Q_A(r) != 0; for a class with consecutive pivots, G = (1/n) d/du log(W/u^N) at u = 0; at l = 2, G_A = -(11 w_1 + 13 w_2)/3. | Working proof (span uniqueness, multilinear Wronskian expansion with Vandermonde ratio n, branch exponents and degree count at l = 2); symbolic and exact checks (research/tools/bmd_cube_far_ga_symmetry.gp, research/results/bmd-20261004-m/). | [First-order coefficients](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-far-ga-asymmetry) |
| `conj:cube-far-ga-asymmetric` | For every l >= 2 the first-order coefficient G_A of the l-level class A is not symmetric under w_1 <-> w_2. | Conjecture: proved at l = 2; exact asymmetry at w_s = (2s+1)/(s+3) for l = 2, 3, 4, 5 (research/results/bmd-20261004-m/ga-asymmetry.txt). | [First-order coefficients](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-far-ga-asymmetry) |
| `lem:cube-far-sector-decomposition` | On the derivative ladder (y = 1/x, Psi = y^-3 U), at r not in {0,-1} every Taylor coefficient of each of the 4e mixed rows y^(3/2-4e+j)(1+y)^(-7/2) splits exactly as I_0(N) + I_-1(N) (keyhole integrals around rays from 0 and -1, endpoint circles included), while pure rows keep their Taylor sequences; hence Wr_y(Psi^(m))(r) = prod (m+s)! sum over subsets S of the mixed rows of the Casorati determinants D_S, grouped into 4e+1 sector sums by \|S\|. | Working proof: decay O(\|y\|^-3) of the mixed rows at infinity, contour deformation and multilinearity in the mixed rows. | [Far sector decomposition](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-far-sector-decomposition) |
| `conj:cube-far-sector-circles` | For fixed e and l -> infinity, all but O_e(l) roots of the far polynomial W_k = T_(R_l) lie in 4e annuli \|log\|1+x\| - log rho_i\| = O_e(1/R_l), each with R_l + O_e(1) roots, and these roots are simple. | Conjecture from the sector decomposition and Darboux heuristics; exact roots at (e,l) = (1,3), (1,4) show bands of 27 (one circle, R_4 = 28), 67 (two merged) and 32 roots, but bands far wider than O(1/R_l) at these sizes (research/results/bmd-20261004-n/sector-roots.txt). | [Far sector decomposition](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-far-sector-decomposition) |
| `lem:cube-far-x-sector-decomposition` | For every even-peeling step, with F the far blocks other than P_<R_e(x) (dim k' = 1+R_l+4e+4l+4el) and n = R_e: off {0,-1,inf} W_k has the same roots, with multiplicity, as Wr_x(F^(n)) = prod (n+s)! det[c_(i,n+s)(r)] (F contains no polynomial, by monodromy characters); the rows singular at both 0 and -1 are the 4l functions (1+x)^(-5/2) x^(1/2-4l+j); for non-real r, with cuts the rays from -1 and 0 pointing away from r, each splits exactly as c_N = I_0(N) + I_-1(N), so det[c] = sum_(s=0)^(4l) E_s, E_s summing the determinants with s mixed rows taking their I_0 parts. | Working proof: classical derivative identity, monodromy characters, decay O(\|x\|^-3) of mixed rows, contour deformation and multilinearity; numerically sum E_s = det[c] vanishes at the roots of W_(b-1) to 1e-100 and the split I_0 + I_-1 = c holds to 1.7e-29 (research/results/bmd-20261004-p/x-sector-balance.txt). | [Last-step sector balance](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-last-far-sector-balance) |
| `conj:cube-far-x-sector-balance` | For every e >= 2, all but O(e) non-real roots r of the last-step far polynomial W_(b-1) satisfy, with the cuts of lem:cube-far-x-sector-decomposition: for some i in {0,1,2,3}, determined by the circle and increasing as \|t\| = \|x/(1+x)\| decreases, \|E_s(r)\| <= eps_e max(\|E_i(r)\|, \|E_(i+1)(r)\|) for s not in {i, i+1}, with eps_e -> 0, where E_s are the x-side sector sums. | Conjecture: at e = 4, 38 of 48 sampled non-real roots balance consecutive sums with third/largest <= 2.5e-4 (pairs (0,1),(1,2),(2,3),(3,4) on log\|t\| in [0.46,0.64], [0.07,0.15], [-0.33,-0.24], [-0.80,-0.60]); 10 others, against 22 = 8e-10 roots outside the four circles; at e = 2, 7 of 13; split validated to 1e-29 (research/results/bmd-20261004-p/x-sector-balance.txt). | [Last-step sector balance](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-last-far-sector-balance) |
| `lem:cube-far-balance-certificate` | If T = E_i + E_(i+1) + R near a root r of T, all analytic with E_i(r) E_(i+1)(r) != 0, phi = E_(i+1)/E_i, and \|E_i(r)\| \|(log phi)'(r)\| > \|R(r)\| \|E_(i+1)'/E_(i+1)(r)\| + \|R'(r)\|, then r is a simple root; in particular with \|R\| <= eps\|E_i\|, \|R'\| <= eps N \|E_i\|/\|r(1+r)\|, \|E_(i+1)'/E_(i+1)\| <= C N/\|r(1+r)\| and \|r(1+r)(log phi)'\| >= delta N it holds once eps(C+1) < delta. | Working proof: T'(r) = -E_i (log phi)' - R E_(i+1)'/E_(i+1) + R' at the root. | [Last-step sector ratio](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-last-far-sector-ratio) |
| `conj:cube-far-x-sector-ratio` | At the last even-peeling step, at all but O(1) of the roots where consecutive x-side sector sums E_i, E_(i+1) balance, kappa_i = r(1+r) d/dr log(E_(i+1)/E_i) = -(R_e + 7/2) + lambda_i with \|lambda_i\| <= (1-delta)(R_e + 7/2) for a fixed delta > 0, i.e. E_(i+1)/E_i = c_i(x) t^-(R_e+7/2) with slowly varying c_i. | Conjecture: at e = 2 (prediction -9.5) Re kappa in [-9.52, -6.84] at 11 of 12 balanced roots (one at -3.29); at e = 4 (prediction -31.5) Re kappa in [-32.0, -21.4] at 37 of 38, one exception at -417-264i (research/results/bmd-20261004-q/). | [Last-step sector ratio](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-last-far-sector-ratio) |
| `lem:cube-far-sector-polynomial` | In the x-side sector decomposition at non-real r with its cuts, the sector polynomial E(z; r) = det[c] with each of the 4l mixed rows replaced by I_-1 + z I_0 equals sum_s E_s(r) z^s (degree at most 4l) and E(1; r) = det[c(r)], which has the roots of W_k off the branch points; if r_0 is a root of W_k at which z = 1 is a simple root of E(.; r_0), the analytic root z_j(r) with z_j(r_0) = 1 satisfies d/dr E(1; r_0) = -d/dz E(1; r_0) z_j'(r_0), so r_0 is simple iff z_j'(r_0) != 0 (a reformulation). | Working proof: multilinearity in the mixed rows and the implicit function theorem. | [Sector polynomial](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-last-far-sector-polynomial) |
| `conj:cube-far-sector-extreme-laplace` | Hypothesis (refuted at e = 2, 4): each x-side sector sum E_s at the last step is dominated by the Laplace term in which the 0-sector rows take the top (or the bottom) block of columns. | Refutation: at 33 balanced roots (e = 2, 4) neither extreme term approximates E_s in any of 132 comparisons; 112 negligible, 20 comparable or larger by up to 1e130 (research/results/bmd-20261004-r/x-laplace.txt). | [Sector polynomial](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-last-far-sector-polynomial) |
| `lem:cube-far-sector-multiple-integral` | With the x-side sector decomposition at non-real r (k' rows f_i, n = R_e), E(z; r) = (2 pi i)^(-k') times the k'-fold integral over Gamma_1 x ... x Gamma_k' of prod_i f_i(y_i)(y_i - r)^(-n-1) prod_(i<i') (1/(y_i' - r) - 1/(y_i - r)), where Gamma_i is a small circle about r for a pure row and K_-1 + z K_0 for a mixed row. | Working proof: entries as contour integrals, multilinearity in rows, and the Vandermonde det[w_i^s] with w = 1/(y - r). | [Sector gas](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-last-far-sector-gas) |
| `conj:cube-far-sector-circle-count` | For every e >= 2, with the cuts of lem:cube-far-x-sector-decomposition and balance threshold 1e-3, each of the four consecutive sector pairs (E_i, E_(i+1)) balances at exactly R_e non-real roots of the last-step far polynomial W_(b-1); the other deg W_(b-1) - 4 R_e roots are real or unbalanced. | Conjecture: exactly 6 = R_2 per pair at e = 2 and 28 = R_4 per pair at e = 4, every non-real root passing the independent split control after a geometric hairpin guard (research/results/bmd-20261004-t/). | [Sector gas](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-last-far-sector-gas) |
| `conj:cube-far-cluster-ratio` | At the last even-peeling step, at all but O(1) roots where consecutive x-side sector sums E_s, E_(s+1) balance, kappa_s = r(1+r) d/dr log(E_(s+1)/E_s) = -n - 15/2 + 2s + r(4s - 6) + o(1) as e -> infinity (n = R_e); equivalently E_(s+1)/E_s = C_s t^(-n-15/2+2s) (1+x)^(4s-6) (1+o(1)) locally with C_s constant, as predicted by moving one charge between the endpoint clusters of the sector log-gas. | Conjecture from a cluster heuristic: median \|kappa - prediction\| 0.79 at e = 2 (12 balanced roots) and 0.46 at e = 4 (38), against 1.34 and 1.49 for the flat value -(n+7/2); the largest error grows from 4.0 to 5.5, and one exceptional root (research/results/bmd-20261004-u/). | [Cluster ratio law](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-last-far-cluster-ratio) |
| `lem:cube-far-concave-balance` | If nonzero complex E_0..E_K (K >= 2) sum to zero and L_s = log\|E_s\| has all second differences <= -delta with delta >= log(2K^2), then with m the maximizer and m' its larger neighbour, \|E_m'\| >= \|E_m\|/2 and \|E_s\| <= 2 e^(-delta) \|E_m\| for every other s. | Working proof: monotonicity of concave sequences away from the maximum, x >= 1/K from the vanishing sum, concavity bounds at m and m', and x >= 1 - K^2 e^(-delta). | [Sector concavity](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-last-far-sector-concavity) |
| `conj:cube-far-sector-concavity` | At the last even-peeling step, at all but O(e) roots of W_(b-1), the x-side sector sums satisfy log\|E_(s+1)\| - 2 log\|E_s\| + log\|E_(s-1)\| = -4 log(n+1) + 2 log\|r(1+r)\| + O(1) uniformly for 0 < s < 4 (n = R_e). | Conjecture, the r-part from the cluster exponents and the n-part an empirical fit: at e = 4 all 48 sampled roots strictly concave, second differences -16.0..-0.42, deviation median 0.96 (quartiles 0.67, 1.23), gap >= log 32 at 38 of 48; at e = 2, 12 of 13 concave (research/results/bmd-20261004-v/concavity.txt). | [Sector concavity](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-last-far-sector-concavity) |
| `conj:cube-far-certificate-scaling` | At the last even-peeling step, at all but O(e) balanced roots of W_(b-1), the x-side sector sums satisfy eps = \|R/E_i\| = O(n^-4 \|r(1+r)\|^2), eps' = \|R'\|\|r(1+r)\|/(N\|E_i\|) = O(e eps) and C = \|E_(i+1)'/E_(i+1)\|\|r(1+r)\|/N = O(e) (n = R_e, N = n + 7/2), so that, with \|kappa_i\| >= delta N (conj:cube-far-x-sector-ratio), eps' + eps C < \|kappa\|/N and the balance certificate of lem:cube-far-balance-certificate holds there for every large e. | Conjecture: the certificate inequality holds numerically (not rigorously) at all 24 (e = 2) and 56 conjugate-pair (e = 4) sampled balanced roots, log10 margin >= 1.03 and 1.06; median eps 8.8e-5 and 6.8e-7, C median 21.4 and 28.5 (research/results/bmd-20261004-w/). | [Balance certificate at the last step](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-last-far-certificate) |
| `conj:cube-last-far-pair-edge` | Hypothesis (refuted): for every e, each of the 8e far zeros of the integral-class Wronskian G_U = Wr_t(u_1, u_2) of the last-step six-space (prop:cube-last-far-six-space), mapped to x = t/(1-t), has a root of W_(b-1) at less than a tenth of the distance to the second nearest root, so that the 8e+4 edge roots of W_(b-1) would follow G_U. | Refuted at e = 2, 3, 4: 0 of 16, 24, 32 zeros have d1/d2 < 0.1 (smallest 0.12); the zeros lie at \|x\| 1.86..4.69, 2.28..6.03, 2.78..7.55, moving outward with e (research/tools/bmd_cube_last_far_pair_edge.gp, research/results/bmd-20261004-y/pair-edge.txt). | [Last far pair edge](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-last-far-pair-edge) |
| `conj:cube-last-far-edge-circle-ends` | For every e, at all but O(1) non-real unbalanced roots of the last even-peeling far polynomial W_(b-1), the two largest x-side sector sums are an adjacent pair (E_s, E_(s+1)) and the root lies on the same side of \|t\| = 1 (t = x/(1+x)) as that pair's balanced roots: the edge is the fringe of the four sector circles, near t = 1 (three-sector balance) and at their crossings of the positive real t-axis. | Conjecture: same side at 7 of 7 (e = 2) and 11 of 14 (e = 4) edge pairs with adjacent dominant pair, one more pair dominated by (1,3); the exceptions have \|log\|t\|\| <= 0.062 (research/tools/bmd_cube_last_edge_sides.py, research/results/bmd-20261004-z/edge-sides.txt). | [Last far circle ends](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-last-far-circle-ends) |
| `conj:cube-last-far-infinity-newton-edge` | Hypothesis (refuted): for every e, the archimedean Newton polygon of Q(s) = s^D W_(b-1)((1-s)/s), s = 1/(1+x), predicts by its segment lengths the roots of W_(b-1) with \|1+x\| >= 4, so that the edge would be a Newton edge at infinity separable by Pellet's theorem. | Refuted at e = 2..9: predicted 13, 25, 39, 56, 90, 115, 143, 189 against actual 11, 19, 27, 36, 53, 67, 85, 106; the length-one segments have radii ~ a/j (exponential-series hull), the largest predicted radius (e.g. 90 at e = 4) far exceeds the largest actual \|1+x\| (13.9) (research/results/bmd-20261004-z/infinity-hull.txt). | [Last far circle ends](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-last-far-circle-ends) |
| `conj:cube-last-far-edge-sector-certificate` | Hypothesis (refuted): for every e, at every non-real edge root r of the last even-peeling far polynomial W_(b-1), the sector certificate \|sum_(s in S)(E_s' - E_s E_s0'/E_s0)\| > \|R\|\|E_s0'/E_s0\| + \|R'\| (R the other x-side sector sums) holds with S the two or the three largest sector sums. | Refuted at e = 2, 4: it fails at all 16 far-ring edge roots (\|r\| >= 5), where the normalized derivative \|T'\|\|r(1+r)\|/(N max\|E_s\|) is 1.1e-12..1.3e-5 (e = 2) and 1.4e-4..1.54 (e = 4), while 17 sampled balanced roots pass (research/results/bmd-20261004-za/). | [Last far edge certificate](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-last-far-edge-certificate) |
| `conj:cube-balanced-mixed-shape` | Hypothesis (refuted): in characteristic 3, for every cluster sizes M, L >= 3, the saturated mixed block of the balanced simultaneous limit (conj:cube-balanced-simultaneous-limit-normality) consists of an interval of consecutive odd powers of x plus (M-1)(L-1)-1 rows outside it, as at (M,L) = (3,3). | Refuted at (3,4) and (4,4) over F_(3^5) with fixed generic slopes: limits x^11..x^-9 plus x^-13 (one outside row, 5 predicted), and x^17, x^15, x^11..x^-9, x^-13, x^-15 plus one coupled row {13,-11}; the (3,3) control reproduces the six-label limit (research/tools/bmd_balanced_mixed_ml.gp, research/results/bmd-20261004-zk/mixed-ml.txt). | [Balanced mixed shape](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-balanced-mixed-shape) |
| `conj:cube-balanced-limit-generic-classical` | In characteristic 3, for every N >= 6 and generic slopes, the balanced simultaneous limit of the degree-two root-curve space, with clusters of sizes floor(N/2) and ceil(N/2) and one zero slope each, is classical at a generic point: its length-D Hasse jet matrix, D = binom(N,2)+2, is invertible there. | Refuted at seven labels by the [generic symbolic obstruction](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-07-cube-generic-seven-limit-obstruction): over F3(b,c,d,e) the full coefficientwise limit has function valuation 89 and length-23 Hasse rank 22 at every nonzero moving point, with kernel x^-13*(x-t)^24. The earlier scope correction remains valid: finite slope samples did not establish this conclusion. No generic eight-label claim or exclusion of all special slope strata follows. The generic six-label result remains proved. | [Balanced limit at seven and eight labels](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-balanced-limit-seven-eight) |
| `conj:cube-two-cluster-limits-nonclassical` | In characteristic 3, for every N >= 7 and every split of the N branch labels into two clusters (near 0 and near 1, one smoothing parameter, generic slopes), the simultaneous limit of the degree-two root-curve space is nonclassical: its length-D Hasse jet matrix (D = binom(N,2)+2) is singular at a generic point. Mechanism: the limits are monomial or nearly so, and their exponent sets fail the Lucas condition det binom(e,k) != 0 mod 3. | Conjecture: jet ranks 22/23 at (M,L) = (2,5), (3,4) and 26, 29, 28 of 30 at (2,6), (3,5), (4,4), with the exactly monomial limits' deficits equal to their mod-3 binomial rank defects; the six-label control is classical (research/tools/bmd_balanced_limit_n.gp, research/results/bmd-20261004-zm/). The [scope correction](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-07-cube-generic-limit-scope-correction) keeps this as a conjecture: fixed-slope support and rank computations do not establish its generic-slope assertion. The [new symbolic seven-label theorem](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-07-cube-generic-seven-limit-obstruction) proves its generic balanced (3,4) case, but not all splits or all larger sizes. | [Two-cluster limit exponents](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-two-cluster-limit-exponents) |
| `check:cube-three-centre-certificates` | In characteristic 3, degree 2: the three-centre simultaneous limits (clusters at 0, 1, c on the rational conic z^2 - c x^2 = 1 - c, fixed generic c and slopes in F_(3^5)) are classical at a generic point for splits (2,2,2), (3,2,2), (3,3,2), (3,3,3), (2,4,4) (N = 6..10) and have jet rank 45 of 47 for (4,3,3), (3,4,3), (3,3,4); by lem:cube-moving-point-limit-criterion, Delta_(n,2) is nonzero mod 3 for n = 7, 8, 9. | Finite check: research/tools/bmd_three_centre_limit.gp, research/results/bmd-20261004-zp/ (three-centre.txt, three-centre-9-10.txt, three-centre-10b.txt); exact saturation over F_(3^5) completing within precision, jet ranks at three generic points. | [Three-centre limit](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-three-centre-limit) |
| `conj:cube-three-centre-limit-classical` | In characteristic 3, for every N >= 6 some split of the N branch labels into three clusters at centres 0, 1, c (one smoothing parameter, generic c and slopes, one zero slope per cluster) has a simultaneous degree-two limit classical at a generic point; by lem:cube-moving-point-limit-criterion this would prove Delta_(n,2) nonzero mod 3 for every n (statement 2's characteristic-three degree-two slice). | Evidence against at N = 12 (check:cube-three-centre-twelve-none): no split classical at the tested parameters; classical splits exist for N = 6..11. | [Three-centre limit](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-three-centre-limit) |
| `conj:cube-three-centre-multiset-invariance` | In characteristic 3, degree 2, for every N the generic Hasse jet rank of the three-centre simultaneous limit (clusters at 0, 1, c on the rational conic, generic c and slopes, the dummy label in the cluster at 0) depends only on the multiset of cluster sizes, not on their assignment to the centres. | Conjecture: holds on all 28 compositions of 9; deficits by multiset at N = 7..10 recorded (research/results/bmd-20261004-zq/), with a classical multiset at every N = 7..10 ({2,3,3} the only one at N = 8). | [Three-centre splits](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-three-centre-splits) |
| `conj:cube-three-centre-complete-series` | In characteristic 3, degree 2, for every N and every split into clusters at centres 0, 1, c, the three-centre simultaneous limit U is classical at a generic point if and only if G*U is the full space of polynomials of degree < D in the conic parameter m (U a complete linear series on P^1); complete implies classical is immediate (Hasse-Wronskian of 1, m, ..., m^(D-1) is 1). | Corrected (entry-2026-10-04-cube-three-centre-correction): the interval test concerns top degrees of G*U, i.e. ordinariness of U at m = infinity, not completeness; see conj:cube-three-centre-mark-ordinary.
