| `conj:cube-tie-square-window-unit-circle` | For every m >= 2, the square tie-window determinant L_m(c) (coefficients of T^k, binom(m,2) <= k <= binom(m,2)+2m, of T^n (1+cT)^(-3/2), T^n (1+T)^(-3/2), n < m, and ((1+cT)(1+T))^(-3/2)), with the factors c and c-1 removed, has degree binom(m,2) and all roots on \|c\| = 1. | Conjecture: verified at 100-digit precision for m = 2..8 (research/results/bmd-20261006-q/); palindromic with positive coefficients (a Lee-Yang-type property). No contact-window minor has all roots off the circle for m <= 7, so it does not alone give full rank. | [Tie window circle](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-06-cube-tie-window-unit-circle) |
| `conj:cube-tie-window-interlacing` | For every m >= 2, the tie contact-window minor D_m dropping columns binom(m,2)+2m and binom(m,2)+2m+2 (factors c, c-1 removed) has degree binom(m,2)+1 and all roots on \|c\| = 1, strictly interlacing those of (c-1) L_m, where L_m is the stripped square-window coefficient; hence gcd(L_m, D_m) = 1 and the tie window has full rank for every c != 0, 1. | Conjecture: verified for m = 2..7 at 100-digit precision with exact gcds (research/results/bmd-20261006-r/); the implication to conj:cube-tie-window-full-rank is proved; equivalent by Hermite-Biehler on the circle to Schur stability of a complex combination of L_m and D_m. | [Tie window interlacing](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-06-cube-tie-window-interlacing) |
| `lem:cube-tie-window-stability-criterion` | For m >= 2 let W'(c) be the (2m+1) x (2m+2) tie window (coefficients of T^(binom(m,2)+j), 0 <= j <= 2m+1, of T^n (1+cT)^(-3/2), T^n (1+T)^(-3/2), n < m, and ((1+cT)(1+T))^(-3/2)) and Delta_j its maximal minors. If f = Delta_(2m) + Delta_(2m+1) is not identically zero and f / (c^a (c-1)^b), with these factors fully removed, has all zeros in the open unit disc, then W'(c) and the tie contact window have full rank 2m+1 for every complex c != 0, 1 (characteristic zero). | Working proof: the substitution T = cS gives Delta_J(1/c) = +- c^e Delta_J(c) for every column set J, so common zeros of Delta_(2m), Delta_(2m+1) are closed under inversion and cannot all lie inside the disc. | [Tie window stability](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-06-cube-tie-window-schur-stability) |
| `conj:cube-tie-window-schur-stable` | For every m >= 2, Delta_(2m) + Delta_(2m+1) (the two last maximal minors of the tie window W'(c)), with its factors c and c-1 removed, has degree binom(m,2)+1 and all zeros in the open unit disc; Delta_(2m) - Delta_(2m+1), after removing its factors c and c-1, has all zeros outside the closed disc. | Conjecture: exact Schur-Cohn test over Q passes for m = 2..8, with 100-digit root counts agreeing (research/results/bmd-20261006-s/); with lem:cube-tie-window-stability-criterion it implies conj:cube-tie-window-full-rank. | [Tie window stability](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-06-cube-tie-window-schur-stability) |
| `lem:cube-tie-window-kernel-orthogonality` | For m >= 2 and complex c != 0, the Cramer kernel polynomial V_c(x) = sum_j (-1)^j Delta_j x^j of the tie window W'(c) satisfies contour orthogonality against x^(R''+1/2-n)(x+c)^(-3/2), x^(R''+1/2-n)(x+1)^(-3/2) (n < m) and x^(R''+2)(x+c)^(-3/2)(x+1)^(-3/2) around the cuts [-c,0], [-1,0]; sigma(c) = Delta_(2m)/Delta_(2m+1) is its zero sum, f_m = Delta_(2m+1)(1+sigma), sigma(1/c) = sigma(c)/c, and c^(-1/2) sigma(c) is real on \|c\| = 1. | Working proof: Cramer's rule, coefficient extraction as a contour integral with x = 1/T, Vieta, and the inversion symmetry of lem:cube-tie-window-stability-criterion with exponents differing by one. | [Tie window kernel](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-06-cube-tie-window-kernel-orthogonality) |
| `conj:cube-tie-window-wronskian` | For every m >= 2, with L_m, D_m the stripped last two tie-window minors, Q_m = 2c(D_m' L_m - D_m L_m') - D_m L_m equals (c-1) R_m with R_m having no zero on \|c\| = 1; equivalently (D_m, L_m being palindromic, checked exactly for m <= 6) the theta-Wronskian of the real functions e^(-i(d+1)theta/2) D_m, e^(-i d theta/2) L_m vanishes on (0, 2 pi) nowhere, so their zeros there strictly interlace. | Conjecture: verified exactly for m = 2..6 (Cayley-transform gcd certificate: no zero of R_m on \|c\| = 1; R_m irreducible of degree 2 binom(m,2), numerically half its zeros inside the circle; research/results/bmd-20261006-t/). | [Tie window kernel](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-06-cube-tie-window-kernel-orthogonality) |
| `lem:cube-tie-window-circle-crossing` | For every m >= 2 and non-integer lambda > 0 (exponent lambda in place of 3/2 in the tie window): every zero of f = Delta_(2m) + Delta_(2m+1) on \|c\| = 1 other than c = 1 is a common zero of these two minors; on an interval of non-integer lambda with constant stripped powers a, b of c, c-1, constant degree of f~ = f/(c^a(c-1)^b), and no common zero of the two minors on the circle minus {1}, the number of zeros of the stripped f in the unit disc is constant, so stability at one exponent propagates. | Working proof: reality of c^(-1/2) sigma on the circle for every real lambda (inversion symmetry and kernel lemma), then Hurwitz continuity of zeros. | [Tie window crossing](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-06-cube-tie-window-circle-crossing) |
| `conj:cube-tie-window-stable-all-exponents` | For every m >= 2 and every non-integer lambda > 0, Delta_(2m) + Delta_(2m+1) of the exponent-lambda tie window, stripped of c and c-1, has all zeros in the open unit disc. | Conjecture: exact Schur-Cohn tests pass for m = 2..5 and lambda in {1/10, 1/2, 9/10, 11/10, 13/10, 3/2, 17/10, 5/2, 7/2, 13/3} (40 cases, research/results/bmd-20261006-u/); generalizes conj:cube-tie-window-schur-stable. | [Tie window crossing](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-06-cube-tie-window-circle-crossing) |
| `lem:cube-tie-window-four-term-stability` | For every m >= 2, with d = binom(m,2), S = m^3+m^2-1, A = m^2+m+1, B = 2m+1, the polynomial g_m = ((S+A)/2) c^(d+1) + ((S-A)/2) c^d + ((S+B)/2) c + (S-B)/2 has all d+1 zeros in the open unit disc. | Working proof: on \|c\| = 1, \|c^d(alpha c+beta)\|^2 - \|gamma c+delta\|^2 = ((A^2-B^2)/2)(1-cos theta) >= 0 with g_m(1) = 2S != 0, so the symmetric Rouche theorem compares g_m with c^d(alpha c+beta). | [Tie window log limit](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-06-cube-tie-window-log-limit) |
| `conj:cube-tie-window-log-limit-closed-form` | For every m >= 3 the lambda -> 0 limit of the tie-window stability polynomial, Delta_(2m) + Delta_(2m+1) of the matrix of T^n log(1+cT), T^n log(1+T) (n < m) and log(1+cT) log(1+T) on columns binom(m,2)..binom(m,2)+2m+1, equals a nonzero constant times c^a (c-1)^b g_m, with g_m the four-term polynomial of lem:cube-tie-window-four-term-stability. | Conjecture: exact for m = 3..7 (research/results/bmd-20261006-v/); the cubic coefficients were fitted to these five values, so each fit is tested by one extra value. | [Tie window log limit](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-06-cube-tie-window-log-limit) |
| `conj:cube-tie-window-log-minor-closed-forms` | For every m >= 3, d = binom(m,2), E = binom(m+2,2), alpha = m(m+1)^2/2, gamma = m(m^2+m+2)/2: the lambda -> 0 log tie-window minors satisfy Delta_(2m+1) = kappa c^a (c-1)^b E (c^d + 1) and Delta_(2m) = -kappa c^a (c-1)^b (alpha (c^(d+1)+1) + gamma (c^d + c)); hence their sum is -kappa c^a (c-1)^b g_m, the limit tie zeros are the d-th roots of -1, and the limit pair interlaces on the unit circle. | Conjecture: exact for m = 3..7 (research/results/bmd-20261006-x/), with the m = 8 sum confirmed; it implies conj:cube-tie-window-log-limit-closed-form, and the interlacing consequence follows by a short trigonometric computation recorded in the entry. | [Tie window log minors](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-06-cube-tie-window-log-minors) |
| `lem:cube-tie-log-square-orders` | For m >= 1, s >= m, the square log matrix M_(m,s)(x,y) (rows x^(k-n)/(k-n), y^(k-n)/(k-n), n < m, and sum_i x^i y^(k-i)/(i(k-i)), columns s..s+2m) has determinant a binary form of degree (2m+1)s + m^2 + 2m, of exact order m(s+1) in x and in y and of order at least m(m+1)/2 along x = y; hence it equals K x^(m(s+1)) y^(m(s+1)) (x-y)^(m^2) (x^s + y^s), K != 0, once the diagonal order m^2 and the divisibility by x^s + y^s are known. | Working proof: homogeneity; Laplace expansion with Cauchy determinants after reducing the top row to sum_(i>=m) (x^i/i) B_i; Taylor expansion along x = y with a Hall-type count of rational components; degree count. | [Log square binomial](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-06-cube-tie-log-square-binomial) |
| `conj:cube-tie-log-square-binomial` | For all m >= 1 and s >= m, det M_(m,s)(x,y) = K x^(m(s+1)) y^(m(s+1)) (x-y)^(m^2) (x^s + y^s) with K != 0; at x = c, y = 1, s = binom(m,2), m >= 3, this is the square half of conj:cube-tie-window-log-minor-closed-forms. | Conjecture: exact for m = 2..5 and m <= s <= 12 (38 cases, research/results/bmd-20261006-y/); the axis orders are proved by lem:cube-tie-log-square-orders. | [Log square binomial](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-06-cube-tie-log-square-binomial) |
| `thm:cube-tie-log-window-closed-forms` | For m >= 1 and s >= m, on the log window (rows T^n log(1+xT), T^n log(1+yT), n < m, and log(1+xT)log(1+yT); columns s..s+2m+1): det N = K x^(ms) y^(ms) (x-y)^(m^2) for the single-log block N; the square minor is (-1)^(s+m)(m-1)! B(s,m+1) (s+m)!/(s+2m)! x^m y^m (x^s+y^s) det N; and the second minor over the square minor is -(s(x^(s+1)+y^(s+1)) + m(s+m+1)(x+y)(x^s+y^s))/((s+2m+1)(x^s+y^s)). At s = binom(m,2), m >= 3, this proves the closed forms of the lambda -> 0 tie-window minors. | Working proof: the functional E -> coefficient of T^N in (1+xT)^m (1+yT)^m E^(m) kills the single-log rows and takes Beta-function values on the product row, giving column operations; det N by Laplace/Cauchy axis orders and an Andreief integral with V(u)^2 for the diagonal order; exact checks in 125 cases, including part 2's constant. | [Tie log-limit theorem](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-06-cube-tie-log-limit-theorem) |
| `thm:cube-tie-window-general-functional` | For non-integer lambda > 0, m >= 1, s >= m-1, N = s+2m, rows T^n (1+xT)^(-lambda), T^n (1+yT)^(-lambda) (n < m) and ((1+xT)(1+yT))^(-lambda) on columns s..s+2m+1: with rho_k = Gamma(k+1)/Gamma(k+lambda-m+1), p_i the coefficients of (1+xT)^m (1+yT)^m, t_k those of ((1+xT)(1+yT))^(-lambda) and r_M = sum_(i<=2m) p_i rho_(M-i) t_(M-i), one has rho_N Dsq = r_N det N and rho_(N+1) Dsec + p_1 rho_N Dsq = r_(N+1) det N, with N the single-series block; so where det N != 0 the (2m+1)x(2m+2) window has full rank unless r_N = r_(N+1) = 0, and the contact window loses rank exactly when r_N = r_(N+1) = r_(N+2) = 0. | Working proof: the weighted functional coefficient of T^M in (1+xT)^m (1+yT)^m sum_k rho_k e_k T^k kills every single-series row (rho_k b_(k-n) is a degree-(m-1) polynomial in k times a geometric factor), giving column operations; checks up to sign in 25 and 16 cases. | [Tie window general functional](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-07-cube-tie-window-general-functional) |
| `conj:cube-tie-single-series-block` | For non-integer lambda > 0, m >= 1 and s >= m-1, the 2m x 2m block of rows T^n (1+xT)^(-lambda), T^n (1+yT)^(-lambda) (n < m) on columns s..s+2m-1 has determinant K(lambda) x^(ms) y^(ms) (x-y)^(m^2) with K(lambda) != 0. | Conjecture: exact for the tie start s = binom(m,2), m = 2..6, at four exponents (research/results/bmd-20261007-a/); proved at lambda -> 0 (thm:cube-tie-log-window-closed-forms); polynomiality in lambda reduces its shape to 0 < lambda < 1 (Beta-moment Andreief approach proposed); K(3/2) != 0 is a separate obligation. | [Tie window general functional](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-07-cube-tie-window-general-functional) |
| `thm:cube-tie-single-series-block` | For non-integer lambda, m >= 1 and s >= 0, the 2m x 2m block of the coefficients of T^k (k = s..s+2m-1) of T^n (1+xT)^(-lambda), T^n (1+yT)^(-lambda) (n < m) has determinant (-1)^m s_(m^s) s_(m^(s+m)) x^(ms) y^(ms) (x-y)^(m^2), with the rectangular Schur functions at e_k -> binom(-lambda,k) nonzero by the hook-content formula. | Working proof: homogeneity; Laplace axis orders with binomial Toeplitz determinants identified with rectangular Schur functions (dual Jacobi-Trudi, hook-content); diagonal order m^2 from the substitution z = 1/(1+yT), where the x-rows modulo the y-rows factor through a unitriangular matrix with beta-order sum q + binom(m,2) >= m^2. | [Single-series block](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-07-cube-tie-single-series-block) |
| `conj:cube-tie-window-gegenbauer` | For all m >= 1, s >= 0 and lambda: r_(s+2m)/rho_(s+2m) = kappa_(m,s)(lambda) c^v (c-1)^w t_s(c) for some v, w >= 0 (data suggest v = m, w = 0), where r is the explicit sum of thm:cube-tie-window-general-functional at x = c, y = 1, t_s is the coefficient of T^s in ((1+cT)(1+T))^(-lambda) (a Gegenbauer polynomial in c), and kappa = C_(m,s) prod_(j=-m..m-1)(lambda+j), C rational nonzero. | Conjecture: exact with symbolic lambda for m = 2..7 at s = binom(m,2) and for m = 1..4 at seven starts (32 distinct cases up to powers of c and c-1, research/results/bmd-20261007-c/); equivalent to a weighted Gegenbauer connection identity. | [Tie Gegenbauer](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-07-cube-tie-window-gegenbauer) |
| `lem:cube-tie-window-gegenbauer-consequences` | If conj:cube-tie-window-gegenbauer holds then, for every m >= 2 and non-integer lambda > 0, the tie coefficient is proportional to t_d, d = binom(m,2), whose zeros are e^(2i theta_j) with cos theta_j the zeros of the Gegenbauer polynomial C_d^(lambda), all simple on the unit circle; and the tie contact window has full rank for every c != 0, 1, because t_d and t_(d+1) have no common zero in C^* by the three-term recurrence of ((1+cT)(1+T))^(-lambda). | Working proof: Gegenbauer generating function at c = e^(2i theta); real simple zeros of orthogonal polynomials; descent through the recurrence (k+1)t_(k+1) + (1+c)(k+lambda)t_k + c(k-1+2 lambda)t_(k-1) = 0; contact-window criterion with det N != 0. | [Tie Gegenbauer](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-07-cube-tie-window-gegenbauer) |
| `lem:cube-top-tie-contact-avoidance` | Characteristic zero, non-integer lambda (lambda = 3/2), N = m+2 >= 4: a top-tie F-curve point of M_(0,N+1) (two top roots with cross-ratio c0 not in {0,1} on a four-pointed component with infinity and a node, over a caterpillar chain of the other m roots) lies outside the closure of the contact locus K = {rank A_(R+1) < R} whenever the tie contact window W(c0) has full rank 2m+1. | Working proof: curve selection; normalization as in the caterpillar corollary; rows split into the deep pairs Q (caterpillar minimality), P_c = V B_c, P_1 = V B_1 and the top pair; Laplace and block-diagonal Cauchy-Binet give a unique minimal term equal to a nonzero constant times a tie-window minor. | [Top-tie contact avoidance](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-07-cube-top-tie-contact-avoidance) |
| `thm:cube-single-tie-chain-avoidance` | Characteristic zero, non-integer lambda: an interior point of a tie F-curve of M_(0,N+1) whose dual tree is a chain (k >= 0 singleton levels above a tie level with cross-ratio c0 not in {0,1}, and a caterpillar of m >= 2 roots below) lies outside the closure of the contact locus K = {rank A_(R+1) < R} whenever the tie contact window W(c0) at start binom(m,2) has full rank 2m+1. | Working proof: one translation of the bottom deep root to eps^V centres all levels; induction over singleton levels with the invariant that a column set L has a minor of minimal valuation among sets inside L and above it; each peel adds the M columns above max L, with a unique minimal Laplace/Cauchy-Binet term whose coefficient is a nonzero rectangular Schur Toeplitz minor; the base is the top-tie analysis. | [Single-tie chain avoidance](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-07-cube-single-tie-chain-avoidance) |
| `thm:cube-tie-window-gegenbauer` | For all m >= 1, s >= 0 and lambda: sum_(i<=2m) p_i rho^(m)_(s+2m-i) t_(s+2m-i) = prod_(j=-m..m-1)(lambda+j) c^m rho^(-m)_s t_s, where p_i are the coefficients of ((1+cT)(1+T))^m, t_k those of ((1+cT)(1+T))^(-lambda) and rho^(j)_k = Gamma(k+1)/Gamma(k+lambda-j+1). This proves conj:cube-tie-window-gegenbauer with v = m, w = 0. | Working proof: Riemann-Liouville form (uv)^m D^(2m) G - Pi c^m G = T^(lambda-m) poly with G = I^(m+lambda) F; integration by parts with P = q + h q' and the pairing j <-> m-1-j give a recursion for J_(m,lambda) in terms of J_(m-1-2j,lambda-1); analytic continuation in lambda; exact symbolic checks for m <= 5. | [Tie Gegenbauer theorem](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-07-cube-tie-gegenbauer-theorem) |
| `cor:cube-tie-window-full-rank` | For every m >= 2 and non-integer lambda > 0, in particular lambda = 3/2, the tie contact window (2m+1) x (2m+3) at start binom(m,2) has full rank at every c != 0, 1, and its tie coefficient is a Gegenbauer polynomial with simple zeros on the unit circle; consequently every interior single-tie chain point lies outside the closure of the contact locus K. | Working proof: thm:cube-tie-window-gegenbauer with lem:cube-tie-window-gegenbauer-consequences and thm:cube-single-tie-chain-avoidance. | [Tie Gegenbauer theorem](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-07-cube-tie-gegenbauer-theorem) |
| `lem:cube-geometric-cone-limit-types` | For the geometric cone a_j = s + f(q^j), f = tx + ux^2 + vx^3, and convergent arcs q -> 0, [t:u:v] along which the configuration is separated, all but at most two indices (the integer breakpoints of phi(j) = min(val t + j, val u + 2j, val v + 3j)) have distinct valuations phi(j) and form a caterpillar chain; the limit in M_(0,N+1) is that chain with at most two displaced roots attached in listed ways: own level (caterpillar), a tie with >= 2 deeper roots (single-tie chain), a cherry or three-root level needing a deeper root, or two-displacement combinations. | Working proof: tropical analysis of the three monomials (concave minimum of affine functions with slopes 1, 2, 3, at most two breakpoints, strictly increasing). | [Cone limit types](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-07-cube-cone-limit-types) |
| `thm:cube-confluent-window` | For a not an integer, n >= 1, d >= 0, b - a not in {1-n, ..., 0} and b not in {0, -1, ..., 1-d}, the (n+1)-square matrix of the coefficients of T^i (1+T)^(-a) (0 <= i < n) and (1+T)^(-b) on the columns d..d+n is nonsingular. Hence, at lambda = 3/2, P_j = (1+T)^(-lambda-j) Pol_(<2M) + C (1+T)^(-2 lambda) projects injectively onto any 2M+1 consecutive columns, P_j + P_(j+1) onto any 2M+2, and every space of the pencil between P_j and P_(j+1) onto the 2M+3 cherry window columns. | Working proof: the coefficients of Q(T)(1+T)^(-a) are a hypergeometric term times a polynomial sigma(k) of degree < n; a kernel vector forces Delta^n of g(k) = (b)_k/(a-n+1)_k to vanish, but Delta^n g(d) = mu^(n falling) (b)_d/(a-n+1)_(d+n) with mu = b-a+n-1; triangularity gives Q = 0. | `lem:cube-topup-translation-equation` | In the cherry setting, for 1 <= p <= M-1, the least coefficients W_p of the window Lambda_p and tau°_p of the top-up T_p, as polynomials in the reparametrized roots y', satisfy d_tr tau°_p = -(lambda + 2M - p - 1) W_p (d_tr = sum d/dy'_i); hence conj:cube-topup-flow-identity is equivalent to the vanishing of the translation-invariant remainder tau_p - kappa_(M,p) (D + 2k e1) Hank_k with kappa_(M,p) = -(lambda + 2M - p - 1) c_(M,p) / (2k(M + k + 1)), k = M - p. | Working proof: equivariance of the cross Pluecker vector under dilations about the cherry root (generator e_t -> (lambda+t)(e_(t+1) - e_t), lowering on coordinates), parameter generator -(1/x) d_tr - E on polynomials in y', comparison at x^(A_p) eps^(B_p); consistent with the exact data at M = 3, 4. | [Top-up translation equation](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-09-cube-topup-translation-equation) |

| `conj:cube-triple-joint-operator-exponents` | For every m >= 2 and distinct nonzero a_1, a_2, a_3, the least-order joint recurrence L = sum_(s<=6) P_s(M) S^s of the three pair sequences g_ij of lem:cube-level-window-reduction has degree 6m+6; P_6(M) has exactly the rational roots m-15/2, ..., m-5/2 (simple), and P_0(M) exactly the rational roots 3m-5, ..., 3m-1 with 3m-3 double, independently of the moduli; the remaining factors of degree 6m have no rational roots for generic moduli. | Conjecture: holds at eight points (m = 2..5, two root triples) modulo 1000003 on the grid j/d, d \| 12, \|j/d\| <= 150 (research/results/bmd-20261009-ker/indicial-roots.txt); the roots at 0 follow from the weight recurrence, those at infinity from a heuristic expansion of the Euler integral (moments and the bulk exponent -2 lambda = -3). | [Triple operator exponents](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-09-cube-triple-operator-exponents) |
| `thm:cube-topup-flow-identity-all` | For every M >= 2 and 1 <= p <= M-1, k = M-p, N = 2M-p: the u^(B_p) coefficient of the cherry cross coordinate on the top-up set T_p = [-p, 2M-2-p] u {2M-p} (x = 1, eps = u, lambda = 3/2) is Vand^2 kappa_(M,p) (D + 2k e1) Hank_k with kappa_(M,p) = -(N + 1/2) c_(M,p) / (2k(N+1)), c_(M,p) the window constant of thm:cube-cherry-hankel-form; this proves conj:cube-topup-flow-identity for every M. | Working proof: the window proof's leading-form count and elimination with column N eliminated by (z+e1) z^(k-1) P, Jacobi's complementary minor on [-k, k+1], and Andreief/Pieri (shifted Hankel = sum_S Vand_S^2 e1(S) = D Hank_k/(2k)); the constant agrees with lem:cube-topup-translation-equation; consistent with exact data for M <= 6; reviewed by one fresh-context medium reviewer. | [Top-up identity for every M](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-09-cube-topup-identity-all) |

| `thm:cube-single-shift-schur-hankel` | For M >= 2, 1 <= p <= M-1, k = M-p, N = 2M-p, t >= 1, and L_t the cherry window with its top column raised by t: the least coefficient of P_(L_t) is Vand^2 tau^(t), tau^(t) = c_(M,p) (c_(N-1+t)/c_(N-1)) N sum_(b<=t) alpha_b H_(b), H_(b) = sum_(\|S\|=k+1) Vand(y_S)^2 h_b(y_S), alpha_b = sum_(s=b..t) h_(t-s)(y) V[b,s], V the inverse of the upper triangular U with U[r,r] = N+r, U[r,q] = p_(q-r); alpha_t = 1/(N+t). Hence where H_(0) = ... = H_(t-1) = 0 (e.g. t = 2 on Sigma_k), tau^(t) is a nonzero constant times H_(t). | Working proof (the top-up proof with eliminator z^(k-1) h P, h the polynomial part of z^(M+t)/P, Jacobi's complementary minor expanded along the staircase rows, Cauchy-Binet with Jacobi-Trudi); exact check 30/30 for M = 3, 4, every p, t <= 3 (research/results/bmd-20261009-ket/single-shift.txt); reviewed by one fresh-context medium reviewer. | [Single-shift Schur-Hankel formula](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-09-cube-single-shift-schur-hankel) |
| `thm:cube-schur-hankel-termination` | For M >= 2, 1 <= k <= M-1, y in C^M, H_(b) = sum_(\|S\|=k+1) Vand(y_S)^2 h_b(y_S): sum_b H_(b) z^b = A(z)/prod_i (1 - y_i z) with A = sum_S Vand(y_S)^2 prod_(i not in S)(1 - y_i z) of degree <= M-k-1, so all H_(b) vanish iff H_(0..M-k-1) do (the set Omega_k); Omega_k is invariant under y -> alpha y + c; real clusters with k+1 distinct entries have Hank_k > 0; affine images of the M-th roots of unity lie in Omega_k for 2 <= k <= M-2. | `lem:cube-polygon-raise-selection` | In the cherry setting, for L = {-p..-1} u J with J a set of N = 2M-p nonnegative columns and E+ = sum J - C(N,2), the coefficient of x^(A_p+E+) eps^(B_p) in P_L is Vand^2 tau_L with tau_L symmetric and homogeneous of degree k(k+1)+E+; hence at the M-th roots of unity (centred at 0) tau_L = 0 unless M divides k(k+1)+E+. | Working proof (homogeneity in x y_s, symmetry under exchange of roots, the window's degree); reviewed by one fresh-context medium reviewer. | [Polygon raise selection](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-09-cube-polygon-raise-selection) |

| `thm:cube-ramification-equals-flow-order` | For every M, 1 <= p <= M and every cluster y0 at which the Hankel block containing k = M - p is closed (H_k'(y0) != 0 for some k' >= k; e.g. distinct roots, or k <= d-1 with d distinct values): V_p(y0) has full dimension M + k, its vanishing-order set is O_p(y0) = I(R) with R = ((N_b - i)^i) the rectangle of the Hankel block containing k = k0 + i, and its ramification weight r_p(y0) equals the flow order j_p(y0) = \|R\|. | `thm:cube-cblock-failure-hypersurface` | Characteristic zero, every M, every distinct-root point y* with j = j_F(y*) >= 1 (flow order of the Taylor cofactor F), analytic arcs y~'(s) = y* + s v + O(s^2) and Puiseux x = x1 s^w + ..., x1 != 0: the first-order data (v, x1) on which the C-block's leading space E has positive weight at the mark are none for w < 1/j, exactly the hypersurface dF(y*) v + gamma x1^j = 0 for w = 1/j (gamma = [t^j] F(y*/(1 + t y*)) != 0), and contained in the tangent hyperplane dF(y*) v = 0 for w > 1/j (a proper condition when dF(y*) != 0); at w = 1/j on transverse arcs the leading C-support is exactly {T_0, S_0}. | Working proof: least valuation of the C-block coordinates from wt_0(V(y*)) = j_F and Gale minimality (prop:cube-cblock-spread-bound), the flowed-arc criterion (prop:cube-cblock-flowed-arc), and the Newton polygon of F along the flowed arc (single edge from (1,0) to (0,j)); at j = 1 it is cor:cube-cblock-tie-hyperplane; reviewed by one fresh-context medium reviewer. | [C-block failure hypersurface](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-09-cube-cblock-weight-hypersurface) |
| `thm:cube-two-set-tie-avoidance` | Characteristic zero, every M, cherry-step setting: if the leading C-block support is two sets (necessarily a single exchange S, S - sigma + tau, by basis exchange; any tau > sigma) and the cross block has a unique leader, the limit pair space L0 has weight at most 1 at the mark, its orders lie in [0, R] (either [0, R-1] or [0, R-2] u {R}), and the arc avoids K. | Working proof: by lem:cube-leading-wronskian-sum the Taylor minors on [0, R-1] and [0, R-2] u {R} are sum_X pi_X Vand(X u Z) and sum_X pi_X Vand(X u Z)(Sum(X u Z) - binom(R,2)) up to constants (falling factorials and Jacobi-Trudi); when the first vanishes the second is -alpha_S (tau - sigma) != 0; no transversality hypothesis; matches the recorded control orders 0..13, 15; reviewed by one fresh-context medium reviewer. | [Two-set tie avoidance](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-09-cube-two-set-tie-avoidance) |

| `thm:cube-excess-failure-codimension` | Characteristic zero, every M, cherry-step setting: if the leading C-support and cross support have unions exceeding a basis by e_C and e_U columns (e = e_C + e_U), the arc avoids K if e <= 2, and, when e_C <= 2M+2 and e_U <= R_C+2, it avoids K unless the leading spaces (E, U) lie in a closed subvariety of Gr(R_C, E~) x Gr(2M, U~) of codimension at least 3 (E~, U~ the coordinate spaces on the unions). | Working proof: containment of L0 in the coordinate space X on the unions (dimension R + e, consecutive orders), avoidance unless L0 meets the (e-2)-dimensional subspace W of elements of order >= R+2, and an incidence count over P(W) with Schubert conditions of codimension e_C and e_U; reviewed by one fresh-context medium reviewer. | [Excess failure codimension](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-09-cube-excess-failure-codimension) |

| `lem:cube-frobenius-planted-excess` | For every multi-index n = (n_0; n_1..n_6) with n_6 >= 1 and any power series f_1..f_5, the series f_6 = T^(\|n\|+2) - p_0 - sum_(g<=5) p_g f_g (any p_g with deg p_g < n_g) makes 1, f_1..f_6 admit the form T^(\|n\|+2), so the Hermite-Pade determinants H(n'') vanish on the whole excess-two simplex n <= n'', \|n''\| <= \|n\|+2, while the three-term identity of lem:cube-window-hermite-pade-frobenius (2) holds; with f_1..f_5 the actual triple-window functions at m = 2 the planted system keeps all 431 determinants on the faces below n nonzero, as the true system does, so identity, block pattern and boundary values cannot exclude excess-two blocks. | Working proof: explicit planting and the left-kernel argument of lem:cube-window-hermite-pade-frobenius (1); exact boundary check at m = 2 (results/bmd-20261009-kfn/planted-boundary.txt); reviewed by one fresh-context medium reviewer. | [Padé block lead closed](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-09-cube-pade-block-lead-closed) |

| `lem:cube-effective-filter-sum` | For m >= 1, zeta with 1 + zeta != 0, any K >= \|zeta/(1+zeta)\|, Q = (1+\|zeta\|)/\|1+zeta\|, and h analytic on \|l\| < R' with R' > R > m, h(0) = 1 and \|h - 1\| <= M on \|l\| = R: G = sum_(l<=m) binom(m,l) zeta^l h(l) satisfies \|G/(1+zeta)^m - 1\| <= M [sum_(k=1)^m ((mK+k)/R)^k + Q^m sum_(k>m) (m/R)^k]; uses the Touchard bound T_k(x) <= (x+k)^k from S(k,j) <= binom(k,j) j^(k-j). | Working proof (Cauchy coefficients, the theta-operator identity of prop:cube-triple-window-large-m Step 3, an injection bounding Stirling numbers); reviewed by one fresh-context medium reviewer. | `lem:support-flat-rank` | Support flat rank: B = F_2[x]/(x_i^2 - x_i), psi a functional on B_{<=E}, E >= 1, K(psi) the affine forms b with psi(b g) = 0 for all g in B_{<=E-1}, rho = n + 1 - dim K. If 1 is in K, psi vanishes on B_{<=E-1}. If not, the zero set Z of K is a nonempty flat of dimension rho - 1, psi vanishes on every h in B_{<=E} vanishing on Z, and Z lies in every nonempty flat with that property; conversely vanishing on the degree-<=E polynomials of a flat of dimension s gives rho <= s + 1. The stratum 1 in K (e.g. a top-coefficient functional, rho = E) has no such flat. | Working proof; checked by the reviewer. | [Statement and proof](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/near-half-pc-degree/#entry-2026-10-10-support-flat-formula) |

Hence the kill probability is q(phi) = E_g[(2^(n+1-rho(phi_g)) - 2^(k-1)(1 + [1 in K(phi_g)]))/(2^(n+1) - 2^k)] <= E_g[2^-rho(phi_g)]/(1 - 2^(k-n-1)); when 1 is not in K(phi_g) the row is killed iff the support flat of phi_g (lem:support-flat-rank), which lies in {a_1 = ... = a_{k-1} = 1}, misses the row's flat. The sum of q^m over functionals is not bounded. | Working proof; checked by the reviewer, who supplied the closed form. | [Statement and proof](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/near-half-pc-degree/#entry-2026-10-10-support-flat-formula) |

(b) With kappa the dimension of their dependencies and kappa' that of the functionals in A_3^* killing them all, kappa - kappa' = (n-2)m - N and E 2^kappa' = sum_phi q(phi)^m, q(phi) the probability that a row is killed; so Pr[not regular] <= 2^((n-2)m-N)(1 + sum_{phi != 0} q(phi)^m) - 1. (c) q(phi) = Pr[T_phi(l_1,l_2,.) = 0] for the symmetric trilinear form T_phi; unconditioned this is the bias of T_phi, differing by a term of the generic order. With the bound 3k-3 of lem:trivector-circuit-overlap the union bound diverges from k = 4. Conjectured span bound k+1 (alpha = beta = 1, k_1 = 3): proved for k <= 3; for k = 4, 5 a reviewer's unarchived exhaustive search reports largest spans 5 and 6. | `lem:circuit-gluing-excess` | Circuit gluing excess: for a circuit of k three-spaces over F_2 (lem:trivector-circuit-overlap) with span w and excess e = w - k - 1, if S = S' + S'' with both parts of size >= 2 and the partial sum over S' is the trivector of a three-space Q, then Q is no member, S' with Q and S'' with Q are circuits of sizes \|S'\|+1, \|S''\|+1 < k, and e(C) <= e(C') + e(C''). | `prop:row-algebra-ceiling` | Row algebra ceiling: for a cover of F_2^n by affine subspaces V_r of codimension <= w with indicators R_r, incidence patterns rho(x) in {0,1}^M and I their set: if a polynomial p over F_2 in M variables of degree t has p(0) = 0 and p = 1 on I, then 1 is in C_{tw}; so the PC degree over F_2 is at most w t*(I), t* the least such t. (1) t* <= max number of rows through a point (weaker than lem:violated-rows-ceiling). (2) t* <= 2^(tau+1) - 1, tau the largest 2-adic valuation of the number of rows through a point (tau = 0: odd covers, lem:cover-sum-gap (c)). (3) t* > t iff an odd set of points meets every intersection of at most t rows in an even number of points. Weaker than the static span; a screening condition t* > D/w for a barrier at D. Gives no ceiling near half for dense covers. | Working proof; checked by the reviewer. | [Statement and proof](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/near-half-pc-degree/#entry-2026-10-10-row-algebra-ceiling) |
| `lem:parity-width-degree-bound` | Parity width degree bound: if a CNF has a refutation in resolution over parities (linear clauses over F_2, resolution on a linear form, semantic weakening) of width W, the rank of the negated clause, then its clause polynomials with the Boolean axioms have a PC refutation over F_2 of degree at most W+1: each line is the indicator of its falsifying affine subspace. Likely folklore; no citation located. | Working proof; checked by the reviewer. | [Statement and proof](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/near-half-pc-degree/#entry-2026-10-10-parity-width-comparison) |
| `lem:gadget-lift-degree-bound` | Gadget lift degree bound: if a CNF psi of width m on n variables has a PC refutation of degree d, its lift by gadgets of degree at most gamma on disjoint blocks of l variables, each lifted clause written as a CNF on its block variables alone, has one of degree at most max{m l, (d+1) gamma}; over any field. So degree over N = n l is at most max{m, d+1}/n; for parity gadgets the degree is between d and max{m l, d+1}. Does not cover encodings with extension variables. Likely folklore; no citation located. | Working proof; checked by the reviewer. | [Statement and proof](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/near-half-pc-degree/#entry-2026-10-10-parity-width-comparison) |

| `lem:static-degree-local-gap` | Static degree local gap: for a cover of F_2^n by affine subspaces V_r with indicators R_r, let d_st be the least D with 1 in the static span S_D (the Nullstellensatz degree) and locdeg f the largest degree of f on a row. (a) 1 in S_D' implies deg f <= locdeg f + D' for every f (gluing with the partition of unity 1 = sum R_r g_r). (b) Some f of degree n has locdeg f <= n - d_st (dual criterion). Hence d_st = max_f (deg f - locdeg f). A witness of any degree becomes one of full degree on multiplication by a monomial, so this is a corollary of the dual criterion, not a freer witness. The PC degree is at most d_st. | Working proof; formula confirmed by the reviewer's brute force on fourteen small covers. | [Statement and proof](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/near-half-pc-degree/#entry-2026-10-10-local-global-gap) |
| `lem:closure-dual-criterion` | Closure dual criterion (a rediscovery, in the language of restricted degree, of the pseudo-expectation duality recorded as prop:local-design-criterion): over F_2, with C_D the PC closure of rows R_r at degree D and e = n-D-1: (a) C_D is the least space containing the rows of degree <= D and p B_{<=D-deg p} for each of its elements p; (b) the functional of f vanishes on p B_{<=D-deg p} iff deg(f p) <= e + deg p; (c) 1 is outside C_D iff some odd-weight f has deg(f p) <= e + deg p for all p in C_D; (d) such f has degree <= e on every affine subspace whose indicator lies in C_D, in particular on rows of codimension <= D and on the falsifying subspace of every linear clause derivable from the rows in resolution over parities with all lines of width <= D-1; so a witness certifies parity-resolution width >= D. | Working proof; checked by the reviewer. | [Statement and proof](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/near-half-pc-degree/#entry-2026-10-10-closure-dual-criterion) |
| `lem:two-occurrence-clause-degree` | Two occurrence clause degree (likely folklore): an unsatisfiable CNF with clauses of size <= s in which every variable occurs in at most two clauses has a unit-resolution refutation and a PC refutation of degree <= s over every field: a minimal unsatisfiable subset has every variable in exactly two clauses with opposite signs, and its clause-variable multigraph is a tree, whose leaves are unit clauses. Pure CNF only; not for systems with auxiliary affine equations or for blocks that are relations. | Working proof; checked by the reviewer. | [Statement and proof](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/near-half-pc-degree/#entry-2026-10-10-two-occurrence-clauses) |
| `cor:occurrence-expansion-ceiling` | Occurrence expansion ceiling: for an (r,s,c)-boundary expander (Alekhnovich-Razborov) with v columns, 1 <= r <= m, in which every column has at least d >= 2 ones, rc <= (1-1/d)^(d-1) v + s, so the bound rc/2 of their Theorem 3.13 is at most (1/2)(1-1/d)^(d-1) v + s/2: v/4 at d = 2, 2v/9 at d = 3, decreasing to v/(2e). For mixed occurrence numbers the ceiling stays near v/4. A limit of the method, not of the degree. | Working proof, from the proof of the recorded proposition; checked by the reviewer. | [Statement and proof](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/near-half-pc-degree/#entry-2026-10-10-two-occurrence-clauses) |
| `prop:clause-occurrence-ceiling` | Clause occurrence ceiling: an unsatisfiable CNF with clauses of size <= s and a set H of h variables such that every other variable occurs in at most two clauses has a PC refutation of degree <= h + s over every field (condition on H; the residue is refuted at degree s by lem:two-occurrence-clause-degree). On single-clause blocks it sharpens thm:occurrence-degree-ceiling (h + c_w (v-h) for blocks of arity w); neither implies the other. Consequences: a pure-CNF candidate with no refutation at D has more than D - s variables in three or more clauses; with the averaging of cor:occurrence-expansion-ceiling, rc <= v/2 - h/18 + s, so the unweighted boundary of r-sets charged with factor <= 1 certifies at most 9v/19 + s when every variable is in at least two clauses. | Working proof; checked by the reviewer, who corrected the constant 9/19. | [Statement and proof](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/near-half-pc-degree/#entry-2026-10-10-clause-occurrence-ceiling) |
| `lem:pure-boundary-sampling` | Pure boundary sampling (low significance, likely folklore): a variable is pure in a set I of clauses if it occurs there with one sign only. (a) In a minimal set of clauses implying a non-tautological clause C, every variable pure in the set occurs in C with that sign. (b) Without tautological clauses, under independent inclusion with probability rho a variable with a positive and b negative occurrences is pure in I with probability q^a + q^b - 2 q^(a+b), q = 1 - rho. (c) This is <= 1/2 for a = b, exceeds 1/2 for some rho when a != b (max about 0.528 for {1,2}), and approaches 1 for a = 1, b -> infinity with rho -> 0, b rho -> infinity. No PC degree bound for this boundary is established; (a) concerns resolution. | Working proof; checked by the reviewer. | [Statement and proof](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/near-half-pc-degree/#entry-2026-10-10-sign-aware-boundary) |
| `prop:generalized-method-ceiling` | Generalized method ceiling (conditional on the statement of Miksa-Nordstrom, arXiv:1505.01358, Theorem 3.8, as rendered by a fetch tool and not read in the text): for a minimally unsatisfiable CNF F = U and E on v variables, with a family of nonempty variable sets of overlap d and Delta the largest number of sets met by a member of U, if the (U,V)_E graph is an (s, delta, xi, E)-expander with xi >= 0 and 1 <= s <= \|U\|, then the method's degree bound (delta s - 2 xi)/(2d) is at most v/4 + Delta/(2d) <= v/4 + w/2, w the most variables in a member of U. In a minimal formula a set with a single neighbour is never a respectful neighbour; the rest is the averaging of prop:two-occurrence-expansion-ceiling. Does not cover non-minimal formulas, among them the method's own applications. | Conditional result: the proof is checked by the reviewer; the method's statement is taken from a rendering. | [Statement and proof](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/near-half-pc-degree/#entry-2026-10-10-generalized-method-ceiling) |
| `lem:copy-normal-form` | Copy normal form: for an unsatisfiable CNF G of width s on n variables, giving each (variable, clause) incidence its own copy and adding the equalities between copies of one variable as affine equations yields a system with every variable in exactly one clause, free dimension n, and PC degree d with deg G <= d <= max{deg G, s}, over every field. So the count of variables in three or more clauses, affine rows not counted, is not necessary in the free dimension. With affine rows counted as rows the branching count is unchanged (h = h_G); the free-dimension form of the branching-density condition is not decided by this. | Working proof; checked by the reviewer, who refused the conclusion first drawn from it. | [Statement and proof](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/near-half-pc-degree/#entry-2026-10-10-copy-normal-form) |
| `prop:two-row-clause-parity-degree` | Two row clause parity degree: over F_2, an unsatisfiable system of clauses of size <= s and parity equations in which every variable lies in at most two rows has a PC refutation of degree <= max{s,1}. A minimal unsatisfiable such system has every variable in exactly two rows; merging linked parity rows into groups (each acting as one equation on its boundary variables), the graph of clauses and groups is a tree, since a cycle gives every vertex its own variable and hence a satisfying assignment; a leaf fixes a variable, and one restricts and inducts. Extends lem:two-occurrence-clause-degree to parity rows. Not proved for blocks that are relations. | Working proof; checked by the reviewer, whose random search of 300,000 small systems found no counterexample. | [Statement and proof](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/near-half-pc-degree/#entry-2026-10-10-two-row-parity-systems) |
| `cor:affine-branching-count` | Affine branching count: over F_2, an unsatisfiable system of clauses of size <= s and parity equations in which all but h variables lie in at most two rows (affine rows counted) has a PC refutation of degree <= h + max{s,1}. So a system with no refutation at D has more than D - max{s,1} variables in three or more rows, in every presentation of its affine part and whatever its free dimension: at D near n/2 a density relative to the free dimension of about one half. Re-derives the branching condition with affine rows for single-clause blocks; says nothing about h/v or relation blocks. | Working proof; checked by the reviewer. | [Statement and proof](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/near-half-pc-degree/#entry-2026-10-10-two-row-parity-systems) |
| `lem:symmetric-period-degree` | Symmetric period degree (classical in content, no novelty claimed): for a symmetric f(x) = phi(\|x\|) on {0,1}^n over F_2, (a) degree < 2^i implies phi(a) = phi(b) whenever a = b mod 2^i (Lucas); (b) if also phi has odd period q on {0..n} and 2^i + q - 2 <= n, phi is constant (Fine-Wilf, quoted from memory). Applied to the imported sextic family (k = 6, m = 1, beta slightly above 1) it reproduces the source's 11/12. For beta >= m the exponent is at best 1 - 1/(2k). For beta < m the moment hypothesis alone, from one row, gives every member the exponent 1/2 + beta/(2m), so the extraction only improves a saving the hypothesis already contains. At D=n, c of degree <=n lies in C iff c\|_Y is in the span P_Y of the unplaced-pigeon indicators; for K+e<=n and K<=n-1 the stacked rank lies between dim V_K\|_S - sum_j dim P_Y^{S_j} and dim V_K\|_S. | Working proof passed by the sole fresh-context medium reviewer; the exact inert range and the top-degree part are its corrections. | [Hole-occupancy kernels](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/common-multiplier/#entry-2026-10-16-hole-occupancy-kernels) |

In particular the matching of [C5] (Ouimet, solution of Talagrand's Problem 5.3) fails the (4,4) condition for every L. | Working proof: McDiarmid gives sqrt N/(8s) exits; conditional on memberships and labels the exits are uniform in their cells, a quarter lie at depth s/4 and move at least s/4 in some coordinate; the level count of lem:level-count-consequence at t=(s sqrt N/(4L sqrt log N))^alpha_j excludes goodness. | `cor:generic-principal-kernel` | Multilinear setting. For an F_p degree-D pseudoideal J containing old Boolean or F_p-domain consequences, w of degree<=b, U<=V_K and errors E_1..E_r of degree<=e, all with F_p coefficients, with b+K+e+(p-1)min(K,e)<=D, stacked rank rho of u->([wE_i u])_i and common kernel N: over F_q with q>rho, a uniform combination E(lambda)=sum lambda_i E_i has annihilator {u in U tensor F_q: wE(lambda)u in J tensor F_q} equal to N tensor F_q with probability >=1-rho/q, and rank rho; so the joint saving is sum rank_i minus one combination's rank. (c) For 1 <= k < L_0 <= n and M >= ((n - L_0)(n + 1) + n)/(L_0 - k), M independent such conjunctions have, except with probability (n - L_0 + 1) 2^(-n), no affine subspace of dimension at least L_0 on which all have degree <= k - 1. (d) A line, a disjunction of r members each a conjunction of k_i >= 1 of K = sum k_i independent uniform affine equations, has falsity indicator prod_i (1 + 1_(Z_i)) of degree exactly K under such A, with no member constant, except with probability (2^K - 1) 2^(-L); (b) and (c) hold for lines with K in place of k. (e) For a CNF F of N clauses of width at most w on n variables and any PCK^1_(F_2) refutation R of size S, weakening and cut give a refutation of size S + O(N M_0 r (w + K n)) in which lines {C, m_1..m_r} on the clauses C that R uses are ancestors of the final line; for M_0 = 1 and every distribution on affine maps with images of dimension at least L >= w + K + 1, some fixed forms leave every padded line below degree K with probability at most (2^K - 1) 2^(-(L-w)); for w + K < L_0 and M_0 >= ((n - L_0)(n + 1) + n)/(L_0 - w - K), except with probability (n - L_0 + 1) 2^(-n), every affine subspace of dimension at least L_0 carries a padded line of degree at least K. | Working proof passed with corrections by a fresh-context medium reviewer in two rounds: (a) by the minimum-distance induction over any field, (b) by surjectivity of B^T and the rank count with averaging over the distribution, (c) by a union over affine subspaces, (d) by expanding the line's falsity into intersection indicators, (e) by weakening and cut (BKZ Definition 11) and a product over disjoint variables. | `lem:nested-word-rank-saturation` | Nested word rank saturation. Let w in Z^d be nested: the positions of its nonzero entries have a non-crossing perfect matching M into pairs u < v with w_u = -w_v (zero entries are singletons); fix M. Let X_1..X_d be disjoint sets of noncommuting variables with \|X_i\| = 2^\|w_i\|. Define the factor sequence S(w): the empty word gives the empty sequence, a concatenation of blocks the concatenation of their sequences, a singleton at i the label x_(i,1), and a matched block (u, W', v) with q = 2^\|w_u\| gives, for a = 1..q in turn, x_(u,a), then S(W'), then x_(v,a). The product P_w of the factors 1 + x in the order S(w), a formula of product-depth one with 0/1 coefficients, has ordered set-multilinear projection (the part on the monomials x_(1,a_1)...x_(d,a_d)) whose partial derivative matrix, rows the monomials over the parts with w_i > 0 and columns over those with w_i < 0, has integer entries and determinant 1 over Z in the orders of the proof; so it is invertible over every ring with 1 and has relative rank 1 over every field, F_2 included. The number of factors is s(w) = sum over zero positions of the product of 2^\|w_u'\| over the pairs enclosing them, plus 2 sum over pairs pi of the product of 2^\|w_u'\| over the pairs enclosing or equal to pi. For the words w_Delta of Tavenas-Limaye-Srinivasan (ECCC TR21-094, eq. (5); k >= 1, r >= 3 odd, d' = r^Delta - 1) padded with zeros to length d >= d', s <= d' 2^(k(2^Delta - 1)) + d - d' <= d N^2, N the number of variables. | Working proof passed with corrections by a fresh-context medium reviewer in two rounds: (a) by chain counts, Kronecker products for concatenations and block triangular matrices for matched blocks, with determinant 1 over Z and the adjugate carried along Z -> R; (c) by induction on the matching; (d) by prefix sums of the TLS words, B_(i+1) = 2B_i + k. Computations over F_2 on eight nested words (full rank), committed before their runs. Nested words only; the reviewer's unit-step construction for every path is computed full rank on 135 small paths and unproved. | [Nested word rank saturation](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/#entry-2026-10-17-nested-word-rank-saturation) |

| `lem:path-rank-saturation` | Path rank saturation. Let w in Z^d have prefix sums P_0 = 0, P_i = w_1 + ... + w_i, with P_i >= 0 and P_d = 0 (every path of P_{k,d}). Refine each w_i != 0 into a run of \|w_i\| unit steps of its sign (a zero entry into a marker), a Dyck word matched by the stack; the innermost step of a positive run is its last, of a negative run its first. The factor sequence: a concatenation of primitive blocks and markers gives the concatenation of their sequences, a marker its part's label, and a primitive block (o, W', c) gives, for b = 0, 1 with the pair (o, c) assigned b: the label of o's part if o is innermost in its run, then the sequence of W', then the label of c's part if c is innermost in its run, a label (i, beta) carrying the digits assigned to the pairs of its run's steps. The product P_w of the factors 1 + x in that order, of product-depth one with 0/1 coefficients and s(w) = sum_i 2^max(P_(i-1), P_i) <= d 2^(max P_i) factors (d 2^k for a path of P_{k,d}), has ordered set-multilinear projection whose partial derivative matrix (\|X_i\| = 2^\|w_i\|, rows the parts with w_i > 0) has determinant 1 over Z in the orders of the proof, so it is invertible over every ring with 1 and has relative rank 1 over every field, F_2 included. The proof holds for every grouping of a Dyck word's steps into groups of consecutive steps of one sign. The same holds for every word with P_d = 0 in which no part jumps across zero (no i with P_(i-1) > 0 > P_i or P_(i-1) < 0 < P_i), a concatenation of nonnegative and nonpositive balanced pieces, by transposition and Kronecker products. | Working proof passed with corrections by a fresh-context medium reviewer in two rounds: (a) by induction over Dyck words with groups of consecutive same-sign steps, concatenations giving Kronecker products and a primitive block a block upper triangular matrix whose diagonal blocks are those of the inner word with its first and last groups truncated; (b) by the height of each part's innermost step; (c) by transposition and Kronecker products over the one-signed pieces. Checked by integer determinants on the 112 distinct paths with k <= 3, d <= 5 or k <= 2, d = 6, words with zero entries and a nonpositive piece, and a reversed-order control. Words with a part jumping across zero are not covered; (1,-2,1) and (2,-1,-2,1) have full-rank products, the second found only by search. | [Path rank saturation](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/#entry-2026-10-17-path-rank-saturation) |

(b) for a pair the four choices leave N - \|A cup B\|, \|A cap B\|, \|B minus A\| and \|A minus B\| holes; (c) in characteristic 2, E_A + E_B = S_{A sym-diff B} with S_T = sum_{j in T}(x_1j + x_2j), so J = Ann_C(E_A) cap Ann_C(S_{A sym-diff B}) cap V_K for every pair and every K; | `thm:local-completion-dichotomy` | For nested bipartite graphs G_k0 <= ... <= G_K on X, Y, \|X\| = \|Y\| = n, G_K complete, deficiencies m_k, weights w_k >= 0 with finite partial sums W_j, Gamma the least layered cost sum_{k<K} w_k \|P - G_k\| of a perfect matching and S = sum w_k m_k; at a level k with a maximum matching M_k of G_k and leftover U_k: completion with constant C asks a matching in G_{k+1} inside U_k of size >= m_k - C m_{k+1}; cover asks one matching of G_{k+1} covering U_k. (a) Completion with C < 1 forces m_{k+1} = 0 (at every level: every level above k_0 perfect, Gamma = S); at C = 1, M_k plus that matching is maximum in G_{k+1}; extension by augmenting paths always holds. (b) For C > 1, a family with last deficient level k*, j >= k*+2 and M >= max_{k <= j-2} (m_k - C m_{k+1})/(C-1): adding M disjoint pairs whose edges enter at level j makes every level complete with constant C, with Gamma' = Gamma + M W_{j-1} and S' = S + M W_{j-1}. (c) On the line, X = {1..n}, Y = X + h, h = floor(sqrt n), M = ceil(h/(C-1)) pairs of length d = ceil(e h) at spacing Delta = 2(n + h + d), levels \|x - y\| <= e^(k-1) from any k_0 <= 1 (or all integers), weights e^k: every level complete with constant C > 1, Gamma >= nh + Md - n - M, S <= (e^2(h^2 + Md) + eh)/(e-1), so Gamma/S >= (1 + o(1)) sqrt n (e-1)(C-1)/(e^2(C-1+e)). | `thm:universal-completion-criterion` | (a) For every bipartite graph G, every set U_X of X-vertices left unmatched by some maximum matching and every such set U_Y of Y-vertices, some maximum matching leaves exactly U_X and U_Y unmatched; hence, for nested bipartite graphs with deficiencies m_k, completion asked for every maximum matching of G_k (a matching inside its leftover in G_{k+1} of size >= m_k - m_{k+1}) holds iff every such pair spans a matching of that size in G_{k+1}, and fails at a level with m_{k+1} < m_k where some pair spans no edge of G_{k+1}. (b) For fixed 0 < r_1 < r_2, independent samples of n i.i.d. uniform points of [0, n] and the graphs of pairs within r_1 and r_2, with a, b, delta > 0, delta <= a, a + 2 delta < r_1 < b - 2 delta, b + 2 delta < r_2 < 2a + b - 2 delta, an offset c > r_2 + delta, a window length W > max(4, c + 2a + b + delta + r_2) and p_n = (n(n-1)(2 delta/n)^2 (1 - W/n)^(n-2))^2, for n > 2W this universal form fails at the first with probability at least 1 - 1/(floor(n/W) p_n) (an isolated open four-point gadget in a window, by a second moment, the window events negatively correlated); at r_1 = 1, r_2 = e, W = 10 the bound is below 1 from n = 4.8517e13. (c) For independent samples of N i.i.d. uniform points of [0,1]^2, s = L sqrt(log N/N) and L > 1/sqrt(2), with probability tending to one no point has at most three points of the other sample within s in both coordinates, so no bipartite graph containing those pairs has a component of at most four vertices. | Working proof: (a) by the components of the union of two maximum matchings, a parity argument excluding the one conflicting path; (b) by a per-component bound on leftover matchings, the exact window probabilities, the factor 1 - W^2/(n-W)^2 and Chebyshev; (c) by binomial tails and a union bound over the 2N points, counting only the other sample, with the boundary points counted separately. | [Universal completion fails on random lines](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/ultimate-matching/#entry-2026-10-17-universal-completion-criterion) |
| `lem:top-coefficient-quotients` | Top coefficient quotients. Over a commutative ring R, let d in R[z] have degree b and a unit leading coefficient, and f in R[y][z] have z-degree at most b+D. The quotient h of f by d (f = dh + r, deg r < b; h = f/d when d divides f) is h = sum_{j<=D} z^j sum_{i=j}^{D} mu_{i-j} f_{b+i}, with 1/d = sum_rho mu_rho z^(-b-rho): a fixed linear combination of the top D+1 coefficients of f. For f = sum_a prod_{j<=q_a} (u_aj + c_aj z), Z_a the factors with c_aj nonzero, m_a = \|Z_a\|, f_s = sum_a sum_{T subset Z_a, \|T\| = s} prod_T c_aj prod_(not T) u_aj, so each h_j is a sum of at most (D+1) p Q^min(E+D, b+D) products of q_a factor formulas, depth delta_0+2, where E = max_a max(0, m_a - b - D) is the excess. For affine u_aj, constant c_aj and d = (z^2+z)^k, mu_rho = (-1)^rho binom(k+rho-1, rho) and each h_j is a Sigma-Pi-Sigma formula of size O((D+1) Q^(E+D) S) at every k, polynomial at bounded E+D; at D <= 1 and E = 0, h_1 = f_{2k+1} and h_0 = f_{2k} - k f_{2k+1}, over F_2 with binary affine factors h_0 = sum_{m_a=2k} U_a + sum_{m_a=2k+1} U_a (e_{1,a} + k), U_a the product of the factors without z. | Working elementary proof passed with corrections by a fresh-context medium reviewer in two rounds: (a) by the quotient as the polynomial part of f/d at infinity, needing only a unit leading coefficient; (b) by expanding the products and counting subsets, N <= (D+1) p Q^min(E+D, b+D); (c) over every commutative ring with mu_rho = (-1)^rho binom(k+rho-1, rho) and the regime formulas, checked by hand on prop:primitive-triple-contact's family at M = 2^t, on f = B^k(z+y) and on the previous entry's k = 1 instance. Part (a) is classical; no lower bound. | [Top coefficient quotients](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/#entry-2026-10-17-top-coefficient-quotients) |
| `prop:frobenius-pair-obstruction` | Frobenius pair obstruction. Let G in F_2[y][z] have a Boolean point where G is 1 at z = 0 and at z = 1, and one where G(y,0) differs from G(y,1). Then no product P of binary affine factors makes G + P divisible by z^2+z (so by (z^2+z)^k, k >= 1): the first point forces P to have no factor carrying z, the second then gives P(y) two values. In particular prod_{i<=n} (z+y_i)^M + z^(nM) + P is never divisible, for every n >= 2 and M >= 1; it fails at n = 1 (P = y_1^M, M a power of two, gives zero) and at M = 0. | Working elementary proof by two evaluations at Boolean points, passed by the same fresh-context medium reviewer in its second round, including the use of n >= 2 and M >= 1 and the n = 1 and M = 0 failures. | [Top coefficient quotients](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/#entry-2026-10-17-top-coefficient-quotients) |
| `lem:interpolation-locality` | In [C5]'s real planar flow interpolation (its Lemma 2.10, flows f and h on the m x m grid with div f = div h and \|\|h\|\|_inf <= U, g = h + rot grad of the McShane extension of the circulation's potential restricted off the set B where the maximal function of \|p\| exceeds U), g agrees with f off a set E_B of at most 4\|B\| <= 4L \|\|f\|\|_2^2/U^2 edges; so for every u >= 0 the numbers of edges with load above u differ by at most that, and for every Phi >= 0, sum_e Phi(\|g_e\|) >= sum over e outside E_B of Phi(\|f_e\|). In [C5]'s setting (f electrical, U = LNRs), with probability tending to one, E_B is a fraction O((log N)^(-1/2)) of the edges, so at levels t <= (1/2 - eps) log log N the psi_4 counts of f and g agree up to a factor 1 + o(1), a failure by a factor 1 + delta transferring either way; above those levels neither direction is controlled, and every edge with \|f_e\| > U lies in E_B. The agreement is deterministic; only the size holds with probability tending to one. Not covered: the integral version (2.30), an optimal vertex of a linear program. | Working proof: g - f = rot grad(psi~ - psi), which by [C5]'s proof of Lemma 2.9 vanishes off the edges incident to B, at most 4\|B\|, and [C5]'s (2.28) bounds \|B\|; the counts and the Orlicz inequality follow; the fraction from [C5]'s (2.3), (2.6) and (2.16), which hold with probability tending to one. | [Flow interpolation changes few edges](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/ultimate-matching/#entry-2026-10-17-interpolation-locality) |
| `thm:electrical-flow-obstruction` | For L > 0, s = L sqrt(log N/N), eps in (0, 1/2], grids of k x k cells of side delta = 1/k with delta <= N^(-eps) and N delta^2 >= 1 (the reduction's grids, delta <= s/32 and N delta^2 >= 16 log N, among them for every eps < 1/2), X_1..X_N i.i.d. uniform with cell counts n_Q, the electrical flow theta (least squares, unit conductances on the cell graph, outflow n_Q - N delta^2), K' >= 1, lambda' in [N/K', K'N] and a coordinate j with alpha_j in (2, infinity], or alpha_j = 2 when L < sqrt(eps)/(pi^2 K') (logarithms natural): for every C > 0 there is c(C, L, K', eps, alpha_j) > 0 with P(lambda' delta^2 sum over edges e of coordinate j of psi_alpha_j(\|theta_e\|/(delta lambda' s)) > C N) >= c for all large N. So the electrical flow's flow-bound value is not O(N) with probability tending to one at any pair of the curve, nor is that of any finite sequence of divisible-sandpile stages with equal splitting on the cell graph carrying the counts to N delta^2, which is the same flow. Per-edge variance: N delta^2 \|\|w_e\|\|^2 with \|\|w_e\|\|^2 >= ln k/(2 pi^4) on a fraction about 8/pi^7 of the edges (free-boundary spectral sum). Uses the imported Berry-Esseen theorem. | Working proof: theta_e is an i.i.d. sum of w_e(Q(X_i)) with \|w_e\| <= 1 (acyclic unit flows); an exact free-boundary spectral sum bounds the mean of \|\|w_e\|\|^2 over edges below by ln k/pi^4 and every one above by (pi^3/16) ln k + 6; Berry-Esseen gives each good edge a Gaussian tail of normalized spread at least sqrt(eps/(2 pi^4))/(K' L); a reverse Markov step on the exceeding fraction gives probability bounded below; psi_alpha with alpha > 2 beats the Gaussian tail. A numerical check of the spectral bounds at k = 8..128 is in research/results/ultimate_matching_electrical_flow_20261017/spectral-check.txt. | [The electrical flow fails above exponent two](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/ultimate-matching/#entry-2026-10-17-electrical-flow-obstruction) |
| `thm:linear-flow-obstruction` | For L > 0, s = L sqrt(log N/N) (logarithms natural), K' >= 1, eps in (0, 1/2), exponents alpha_1, alpha_2 in (2, infinity), grids of k x k cells of side delta = 1/k with delta <= N^(-eps) and N delta^2 -> infinity, X_1..X_N i.i.d. uniform with cell counts n_Q, lambda' in [N/K', K'N], and every linear flow rule W (a linear map from mean-zero cell vectors rho to edge flows with div W rho = rho, fixed before the points, possibly depending on N and the grid), with flow theta = W(n - N delta^2): for every C > 0 there is c(C, L, K', eps, alpha_1, alpha_2) > 0 with P(lambda' delta^2 sum_e psi_alpha_d(e)(\|theta_e\|/(delta lambda' s)) > C N) >= c for all N beyond a threshold depending only on the grid sequence and these constants, c and the threshold uniform in W. So no linear rule has flow-bound value O(N) with probability tending to one at any pair of the curve other than its endpoints; the electrical flow, the equal-splitting sandpile sequences and, on grids with k a power of two and dyadic depth at least log_2 k, the dyadic flow written as grid fluxes are such rules. Uses the imported Berry-Esseen theorem. | Working proof: theta_e is an i.i.d. sum of W_e(Q(X_i)); Thomson's principle per column bounds the total second moment below by the electrical one, at least 2k(k-1) ln k/pi^4 by thm:electrical-flow-obstruction's spectral sum; a coordinate carrying half and its edges with M_e >= ln k/(2 pi^4); the Berry-Esseen ratio is at most 1/sqrt(N delta^2) for every rule since max \|W_e\| <= \|\|W_e\|\|; weighted thresholds u sqrt(r_e) with psi_alpha(u sqrt r) >= r psi_alpha(u); a weighted reverse Markov step. | [Linear flow rules fail when both exponents exceed two](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/ultimate-matching/#entry-2026-10-17-linear-flow-obstruction) |
| `lem:restoring-drift-tail` | For alpha >= 1, kappa, sigma > 0, d with d(r) between 0 and r and \|d(r)\| >= min(kappa \|r\|^(alpha-1), \|r\|), and R_0 = 0, R_(n+1) = R_n - d(R_n) + xi_(n+1) adapted with E[exp(t xi_(n+1)) \| F_n] <= exp(sigma^2 t^2/2) for every real t: for every n >= 1 and u > 0, (a) P(\|R_n\| >= u) <= 2 exp(-u^2/(2 n sigma^2)); (b) P(\|R_n\| >= u) <= 2n exp(-min(kappa (u/2)^alpha, (u/2)^2/2)/sigma^2). With n sigma^2 = s^2 fixed, kappa = c sigma^2 ln n, n >= 2: for u with c (u/2)^alpha >= 2 and c ln n (u/2)^(alpha-2) <= n/(2 s^2), P(\|R_n\| >= u) <= 2 exp(-(c/2) ln n (u/2)^alpha), a psi_alpha-type tail with constants independent of n on a window of u growing like (n/ln n)^(1/(alpha-2)) for alpha > 2. | Working proof: (a) cosh(t R) grows by at most exp(sigma^2 t^2/2) per step since the drift does not increase \|R\|; (b) exp(theta R) with theta = 2 min(kappa (u/2)^(alpha-1), u/4)/sigma^2 is a supermartingale while R >= u/2, and a last-exit decomposition over the n steps; the lower tail from -R_n, which follows the recursion with -d(-r). The form for every u was the reviewer's suggestion, checked by hand. | [A paired restoring drift amplifies tails](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/ultimate-matching/#entry-2026-10-17-restoring-drift-construction) |
| `lem:sibling-exchange-leg` | For a closed rectangle B, a segment Gamma of its top side of length l, and a piecewise C^1 field w with continuous normal components near B, with div w = 0 on each piece and w.n = 0 on the boundary of B off Gamma: int_B w_1 = int_Gamma (x - c) w_2 dx for every real c, so \|int_B w_1\| <= (l/2) int_Gamma \|w_2\| dx. Hence a divergence-free correction on two stacked squares of side rho with zero normal flux on their outer boundary that shifts the lower square's horizontal mean by m has (1/rho) int over their shared side of \|w_2\| >= 2\|m\|; the same with the coordinates exchanged. | Working proof: div(x w) = w_1 when div w = 0, the divergence theorem summed over the pieces, and the zero net flux through Gamma. Elementary. | [A paired restoring drift amplifies tails](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/ultimate-matching/#entry-2026-10-17-restoring-drift-construction) |
